blocks.text: The Singson Dynasty
A timeline mapping the notable rotation and overlap of local government positions held by the Singson family across three decades.
Scroll or swipe right to see the dynasty’s full timeline. Tap or hover a bar for details, including family ties and each member’s years in power.
Source: Comelec, public records

Attempts to challenge the family have failed. In 2019, Chavit beat long-time rival Edgardo Zaragoza for mayor. In 2023, Chavit then filed graft charges against Zaragoza and his relatives over the alleged misuse of P81 million in tobacco excise tax funds.

When Chavit backed out of his reelection bid for governor in 2013, his son, Ryan Luis, replaced him. He was challenged by former ally and aide of Chavit, Roque Verzosa Jr. Verzosa filed a case against Ryan Luis for vote-buying after he supposedly gave out at least P20,000 during a fiesta event. Yet the elections ended with the same result: the Singsons still dominated the region.

blocks.caption: FATHER-SON. Ryan Luis Singson with his father Luis ‘Chavit’ Singson in 2013. Photo courtesy of Ryan Luis Singson’s official facebook page

blocks.text: In 2011, Ronald, Chavit’s other son, resigned as congressman after pleading guilty to drug trafficking in Hong Kong and was detained by authorities for 11 months. Ryan Luis, who was vice mayor of Vigan at the time, defeated Liberal Party candidate lawyer Beltrand Baterina in a special congressional election.
Then-councilor Lourdes Baquiran replaced Ryan Luis for the vice mayoral seat after his win.

The family also operates as a politicontractor. Their construction firm, Satrap Construction, secured P2.1 billion in infrastructure projects in Ilocos Sur from 2016 to 2025. They have ties, too, to DITO Telecommunity Corporation and entered the transportation sector to produce electric vehicles.

The family’s power did not just rely on politics. It required money and carefully thought-out moves that favored them. When the Singsons took control of the region in the 1970s, the family divided power.
Titong II replaced his brother Chavit as governor. Another brother of theirs, Jerry, became a councilor and eventually a provincial board member.

Chavit’s niece, Eva Marie Singson-Medina, became a provincial board member in 1992 and Vigan mayor from 1995 to 2004. The patriarch’s son, Randolf, became councilor for multiple terms. The influence extended to their cousins, who won seats in other towns.

Chavit also fulfilled his promise of passing Republic Act No. 7171, which mandates the allocation of excise tax on locally manufactured cigarettes for the benefit of local government units (LGUs) and tobacco farmers. This became a regular revenue for the region.
But his biggest political move happened in 2000.

Chavit’s friendship with then-president Erap Estrada fell apart after Estrada gave a gambling license to Chavit’s cousin and rival, Eric. In a press conference, Chavit exposed Estrada’s link to jueteng, accusing him of taking P130 million from the tobacco excise tax share of Ilocos Sur.
This sparked a chain of events that culminated in Estrada’s ouster during EDSA II.
In the 2010 elections, Chavit left the Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats for the Nacionalista Party to endorse former senator Manny Villar.

The clan was also careful with its political alliances. Though Chavit joined the Uniteam tandem before, he joined the September 21, 2025 protest and called on students to skip classes and go against the government.
A group claiming to be former Marcos loyalists also pushed for a possible tandem between Vice President Sara Duterte and Chavit in the 2028 national elections.

On September 6, Chavit was also seen arriving at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court at the time Duterte posted bail for three counts of grave threats. However, he said he was only there to allegedly check on the progress of his case and not support the Vice President.
Switching sides and alliances through every election and political rift had just become second nature to the Singson family. And they have thrived. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PISA test reveals alarming drop in reading and math skills worldwide
articles.summary: The influential global study shows a downward trend in students' performances. Germany is faring worse than ever.

image.caption: 760,000 students in 91 countries and economies worldwide took the testImage: Armin Weigel/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The results of the 2025 PISA study, published on September 8, show a dramatic drop in performance in reading and mathematics around the world.

The Program for International Student Assessment, better known as PISA, is a global study that measures how well 15-year-old students can apply their knowledge and skills in reading, mathematics and science to real-life situations. The test is designed to measure problem-solving skills rather than evaluate students on memorized school facts, which means they cannot revise in preparation for it.
First administered in 2000, it is considered the world's most influential measure of educational performance.
In 2025, more than 760,000 students in 91 countries and economies took the test.

The study always includes in its ranking the average of the international group of 38 advanced, high-income countries that are part of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development, the OECD.
Downward trend in students' performances
Between 2015 and 2025, reading skills have seen the most significant decline, decreasing by 28 points in OECD countries, and by 16 points in the other participating countries and economies.
Scores in math have dropped by 22 points across the OECD on average, compared to a decline of 8 points in the rest of the world.
In science, the focus of the 2025 PISA assessment, a 7-point decline was measured in OECD countries, while the performances in other countries and economies remained broadly stable.
Nearly a third of OECD students considered 'low performers'
The latest PISA study reveals that around 29% of 15-year-olds in OECD countries are now estimated to be "low performers" across all three subjects.
What does this mean?

In science, they struggle to interpret simple data or decipher a graph. In reading, they find it hard to find information in simple texts. In mathematics, they might be unable to understand, for example, the relationship between units and price — basic skills needed for grocery shopping.
Drop in global reading scores most concerning
Across the OECD, reading scores fell by 25 score points on average.
The study points out that 20 score points are about equivalent to a year of learning. This implies that most 15-year-old students were performing at the level typically expected of 14-year-olds.
Among the OECD countries, the drops were most extreme in Iceland and Slovenia, with scores going down by more than 50 points.

Reading scores improved in five countries only: Qatar (up 11 points), Brunei Darussalam (18), Cambodia (26), the Philippines (27) and Zambia (50). Even though these education systems are still below the OECD average, they "deserve recognition for achieving measurable gains despite the broader global decline," notes the study.
Not all schools are equal in Germany
In some countries, such as Iceland, Cambodia and Finland, for example, there is very little variation in performance among schools, showing less than 10% overall variation in student achievement.
But in 10 countries, including Germany, differences among schools account for at least 50% of the total variation in performance.

The study notes that these countries' systems presumably have schools reserved for higher-achieving students, leaving disproportionately large numbers of lower-achieving students enrolled in the other institutions.

For the authors of the PISA study presentation, this is a problem that needs to be taken seriously: "Where such academic segmentation compounds with social background, it can amplify inequalities, producing pockets of excellence while failing to ensure consistent learning outcomes across the education system as a whole."
Germany's PISA shocks
The very first PISA study was held in the year 2000. As one of the 31 participating countries, Germany was shocked to discover that its 15-year-olds scored below the international average.
In the last PISA test, held in 2022 and published in 2023, the scores of German students had dropped to a new low.
In the latest study, scores have plunged even deeper.
Between 2022 and 2025, reading scores plummeted by 15 points and math scores by 11 points, while science scores have gone down by 7.

The top 6 rankings in reading skills are held by Asian countries. Germany barely remains above the OECD average, coming in 23rd. The United States comes in 13th position; Poland ranks 14th and Turkey 16th.
In math, Germany is below the OECD average, coming in 26th, just a rank above the United States. All top 7 positions are held by Asian countries, followed by Estonia in the 8th spot.

In science, Germany is only 2 score points above the OECD average, ranking 23rd. Turkey made important progress in this field, now ranking 19th, with an increase of 18 score points since the 2022 study.

blocks.caption: The PISA study also asked about students' boredom in class and their use of AI in schoolworkImage: Armin Weigel/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Why is educational performance falling globally overall?

The data itself cannot explain the decline in reading skills, but the authors of the study note that while school closures due to COVID-19 may be one factor, there is no direct relationship between how long schools closed during the pandemic and the students' performances in reading.
There was already a downward trend in many countries long before the pandemic struck, the study notes.

These long-term declines in skills "suggest deeper structural issues within education systems, with challenges at the school and system level," says the study. These challenges include the impact of digital distractions on students and growing disinterest towards reading books.

blocks.caption: Cell phones and social media have an impact on the popularity of reading booksImage: Disobeyartphotograph/Dreamstime/IMAGO

blocks.text: AI has had an immediate impact on learning. The 2025 PISA study asked students about their use of AI in schoolwork; more than 40% said they used it to draft texts for writing assignments once or twice a week, or even every day. Students who reported using AI chatbots got lower scores in science, on average, than those who didn't use AI.

"Overall, the data suggests weaknesses in how education systems are adapting to social, technological and economic change," states the study's summary. "Looking ahead, the challenge for policymakers is not simply recovering lost ground, but to ensure schools meet the rapidly changing demands of the world. As PISA shows, it is not an easy task."

While waiting for policymakers to react, the study suggests that parents can contribute to children's potential by being supportive and curious about their studies and helping them develop positive attitudes towards school. "Even something as simple as asking children what they learned or did at school, about once a week or more, is associated with an average 26-point increase in science performance, after accounting for socio-economic status."

articles.title: PH-Malaysia military ties remain strong amid EDCA concerns
articles.summary: PH-Malaysia military ties remain strong amid EDCA concerns

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 3:28pm

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said its relationship with Malaysia remains strong amid concerns raised by Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim over the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) site with the United States in Palawan.
At a press briefing, AFP spokesperson for West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad acknowledged the geographic proximity of Palawan's Balabac area to Malaysia's Sabah.

“Geography is a constant. Balabac is close to Malaysia. That's a given. The AFP and the Malaysian Defence Forces have very strong military-to-military relationships. We have a lot of engagements with them,” Trinidad said.

“The actions of the Philippines, when it comes to our defense and security matters, are actions of a sovereign state designed to give us more leverage in executing our mandate of securing and protecting our territory against any foreign threat that is currently encroaching into our maritime domain,” he added.
For matters involving the diplomatic side of the issue, Trinidad said the AFP would defer to the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA).
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in August expressed concerns over the EDCA site in Palawan.

EDCA, signed in 2014, grants US troops access to designated Philippine military facilities, the right to construct facilities, and preposition equipment, aircraft, and vessels, but rules out permanent basing.
There are currently nine EDCA sites in the country:

items: Antonio Bautista Air Base (Palawan)
Basa Air Base (Pampanga)
Fort Magsaysay (Nueva Ecija)
Mactan-Benito Ebuen Air Base (Cebu)
Lumbia Air Base (Cagayan de Oro City)
Naval Base Camilo Osias (Sta. Ana, Cagayan)
Lal-lo Airport (Lal-lo, Cagayan)
Camp Melchor Dela Cruz (Gamu, Isabela)
Balabac Island (Palawan)

articles.title: UK commits £100m to bolster Ukraine’s air defences over winter
articles.summary:
Package of military equipment includes Patriot missiles, supplies of which have dwindled amid Russian attacks

The UK has committed £100m to boost Ukraine’s air defences over winter with a…

blocks.text: The UK has committed £100m to boost Ukraine’s air defences over winter with a package of military equipment including Patriot missiles.
Defence interceptors, large-calibre artillery rounds and drones will be supplied to Ukraine through the contribution to Nato’s prioritised Ukraine requirements list.

Supplies of Patriot missiles, which are used to stop aircraft, cruise missiles, and tactical ballistic missiles, have dwindled in Ukraine, causing a drop in interceptions of Russian attacks, according to military experts.

The UK defence secretary, Wes Streeting, is due to co-chair his first meeting of the Ukraine defence contact group, made up of about 50 nations providing military equipment to Kyiv, with his German counterpart, Boris Pistorius, on Tuesday.
The UK recently agreed to declassify blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French-produced version of the Storm Shadow, which has already been used to hit targets in Russia.

Streeting said: “Both the prime minister and I heard loud and clear on our first visits to Kyiv the importance of supporting Ukraine through this winter, as Putin prepares to use winter as a weapon by continuing barbaric attacks against civilian and energy targets.

“We promised to mobilise allies and provide more support wherever we can. Today, we are delivering on that, strengthening Ukraine’s defences and, alongside 50 allies, converting commitment into capability.
“We will stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine until they win. Ukraine’s frontline is the frontline for freedom everywhere and our support will not waver.”

The prime minister, Andy Burnham, spoke to the US president, Donald Trump, about the war on Monday, with the two agreeing on the need to “continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life”.
after newsletter promotion

US envoys held talks in Kyiv on Sunday during an official visit to the country as part of an effort to end the conflict with Russia. While the talks were described as encouraging, no breakthrough was made. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said it appeared the war would continue into winter.

articles.title: One Nation’s Warren Pickering admits to illegal drug use and says he is ‘no angel’ in extraordinary press conference
articles.summary: Victorian One Nation leader tells media he has used methamphetamine, speed and marijuana

blocks.text: The Victorian One Nation leader, Warren Pickering, has admitted he “made mistakes” in his 20s, including using ecstasy, methamphetamines and marijuana, losing his license multiple times for drink driving and hurting people he loved.

But he has denied claims by his ex-partner, published by The Australian, that he smoked ice – also known as crystal meth – in front of children and said he was considering legal action against the publication at a press conference on Tuesday. Guardian Australia and the ABC were barred from attending the press conference.
Accompanied by James Ashby, One Nation’s national director, and his daughter and stepson, Pickering said he was “no angel” as a young man and used illegal drugs in his 20s.
“Never would I have ever said that I was somebody who was a drug addict. I did use them … as a young man and I’m not proud of that,” Pickering said.
He listed ecstasy, methamphetamine, speed and marijuana, but denied using ice or smoking it while his children were home.
“No, I did not,” Pickering said, when asked directly.

blocks.caption: Warren Pickering at the press conference in Melbourne. Photograph: James Ross/AAP

blocks.text: Pickering also confirmed he lost his license three times for drink driving.
“I believe I lost my license for drink driving as an 18-year-old, and again as a 20-year-old, and then probably a decade later, I believe they were low-level drink driving,” he said.

Pickering said his actions “hurt people I loved, and I will live with that forever”. But he said he “changed his life dramatically” for the sake of his daughter and three stepsons, became clean and joined the Australian Defence Force, which he said gave him a sense of purpose.
“That’s what inspired me to engage in the political sphere to provide service to community in a different way, post-service,” he said.
after newsletter promotion

Ashby also spoke, telling reporters a handwritten note by Pickering published by The Australian, which references “sexual deviance”, was in relation to “behaviour that involved the couple’s open relationship”.
“They opened that relationship to a third person, and at the same time, Mr Pickering was exploring his own sexuality,” Ashby said.
Pickering said he was “working with the lawyers” to get the stories “taken” down and was receiving advice about possible defamation action.

Reporters from The Australian were able to attend the press conference at Crown Casino. However, reporters from both Guardian Australia and the ABC were asked by Ashby to leave after identifying the media outlet they worked for.

articles.title: Stranded dolphin rescued in Leyte
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — Local responders rescued a dolphin stranded in shallow waters off Barangay Ul-og in Calubian, Leyte, and safely returned it to the sea on Monday. Personnel from the Philippine Coast…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Local responders rescued a dolphin stranded in shallow waters off Barangay Ul-og in Calubian, Leyte, and safely returned it to the sea on Monday.

Personnel from the Philippine Coast Guard, the Department of Agriculture (DA)-Calubian, and the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) responded after the dolphin was reported at about 1 p.m.
The responders assessed the dolphin’s condition, took its measurements, and guided it toward deeper waters to ensure its safe return to the sea.
The dolphin was in generally good condition, except for a minor wound on its snout that responders said could have been caused by contact with rocks.
They said strong sea currents and winds could have disoriented the dolphin, which was found at low tide, causing it to stray into shallow waters.
The dolphin measured about 5 feet 9 inches long and 10 inches wide, with a body circumference of 32 inches.
After the assessment, the rescue team guided the dolphin back into deeper waters off Barangay Efe and released it./coa

articles.title: Avalanche kills 11 climbers in southern Russia – rescuers
articles.summary: MOSCOW — An avalanche on one of Russia’s highest mountains has killed 11 climbers and left six others missing, rescue services said Monday. Rescuers received reports of the avalanche on…

blocks.text: MOSCOW — An avalanche on one of Russia’s highest mountains has killed 11 climbers and left six others missing, rescue services said Monday.
Rescuers received reports of the avalanche on Mount Mizhirgi, around 5,000 meters (16,400 ft) tall, at around 5 pm (1400 GMT) on Sunday.
Unverified video on social media showed what appeared to be a mound of snow and ice crashing down a mountainside in the area, as people in the background could be heard swearing.
“Tragically, 11 people were killed. The fate of six climbers remains unknown,” the local branch of Russia’s emergency ministry said in a statement.
“Search and rescue operations are being complicated by difficult terrain and the risk of avalanches,” it added.
A group of 33 climbers were in the area at the time.
Ten managed to evacuate on their own, while six had to be transported out by rescue services, according to the local branch of Russia’s emergency ministry.
Prosecutors have opened a case into criminal negligence.
Mount Mizhirgi, near the Georgian border, is Russia’s eighth-tallest mountain.
Surrounded by pristine forest and glaciers, the area is popular with hikers. /dl

articles.title: All NLEX San Simon lanes reopen after flood mitigation measures
articles.summary: MANILA – All lanes on both northbound and southbound portions of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) near the San Simon Interchange in Pampanga were opened on Tuesday, following joint mitigation…

blocks.text: MANILA – All lanes on both northbound and southbound portions of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) near the San Simon Interchange in Pampanga were opened on Tuesday, following joint mitigation measures by the government and the private sector to hasten the receding of floods caused by heavy monsoon rains in recent days.

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon and NLEX President and General Manager Luis Reñon inspected the thoroughfare, where Dizon announced that the areas are now clear of floodwaters.

The DPWH chief said President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. ordered the construction of detention basins at three locations in San Simon, Pampanga, as a long-term solution to flooding, while short-term measures continue to be implemented to prevent a recurrence of the incident that caused a major travel disruption in late August.
He reported that more than 20 units of heavy equipment are set to arrive in the area on Tuesday to begin dredging operations along the Tulaoc River.

“We have a large number of heavy equipment units arriving—more than 20—to conduct simultaneous dredging operations in this area. Most of them are coming from San Miguel Corporation, so I am grateful to Ramon S. Ang (RSA); he isn’t obligated to assist us with this, yet he is doing it. NLEX will also be sending their own equipment to ensure the work proceeds without interruption,” Dizon said in an interview.
Asked when they expect to complete the dredging, he answered, “I can give a timeline later on this week.”
He also acknowledged the partnership with other government agencies and the private sector.
“Coordination with other government agencies and the private sector is very important. The water here is just circulating. Slowly but surely, we will flush it out (into Manila Bay),” Dizon added.
On the other hand, Reñon reported that there is no water on the expressway, and all lanes are now open.

“On a positive note, we can now breathe a sigh of relief as we are opening the third lane of the expressway. There is no longer any water on the expressway; all lanes are now passable, allowing motorists to travel quickly to the north and to Manila,” he said. /gsg

articles.summary: CABANATUAN CITY – Wesleyan University -Philippines (WU-P), one of the largest campuses in Cabanatuan City, denounced the murder on Sunday of one of their scholars at her home in the Nueva Ecija…

blocks.text: CABANATUAN CITY – Wesleyan University -Philippines (WU-P), one of the largest campuses in Cabanatuan City, denounced the murder on Sunday of one of their scholars at her home in the Nueva Ecija town of San Antonio.
Another student, who reportedly discovered the lifeless remains of 21-year-old nursing student Ann Pauline Fajardo, was later apprehended and had confessed to killing her, police said.

The suspect initially claimed that Fajardo had committed suicide at her residence in Barangay Sto. Cristo at 10:30 a.m. on Sunday. “Upon arrival, the responding officers found the victim already lifeless, with the blanket still tied around her neck,” the police reported.
Fajardo’s mobile phone, a P66,990.00 iPhone Plus, was missing. But using the phone’s tracking feature, the unit traced it back to the student who reported to the police regarding Fajardo’s death.
The suspect eventually admitted to killing Fajardo, who was her relative, after she allegedly refused to lend him P5,000 at that same morning.

“We condemn this heinous and unspeakable act in the strongest possible terms. Violence against any member of our community is an outrage to our shared humanity, and we grieve deeply for a bright future cut short so cruelly,” the WU-P said in a statement issued on Monday.
WU-P described Fajardo as “a dedicated student, a cherished friend, and a promising future nurse whose passion, hard work, and kindness touched everyone around her.”/coa

articles.title: Threatening letters revive fears among Kashmiri Pandits
articles.summary: A new wave of threatening letters targeting Kashmiri Pandits has deepened fears among those who have returned to the region as civil servants under an Indian government federal rehabilitation scheme.…

blocks.text: A new wave of threatening letters targeting Kashmiri Pandits has deepened fears among those who have returned to the region as civil servants under an Indian government federal rehabilitation scheme. Kashmiri Pandits are members of the Hindu minority community who fled the Muslim-majority Kashmir Valley during a militant uprising in the 1990s.
The latest letters, which surfaced in the last week of August, named several employees. The letters also included their addresses, vehicle registration numbers and phone numbers.
Personal details exposed

“Similar threat letters surfaced in early August, but the latest contains our Jammu residential address, vehicle and phone numbers, which have also been shared on social media,” Anil Koul, a government employee, told DW, urging authorities to investigate the source of the leak.

The letters have been attributed to a little-known group calling itself the United Liberation Council, which security officials suspect could be a front for the Pakistan-based Islamist militant outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba.

The group reportedly first surfaced in July, when it released a poster marking the death anniversary of a former militant commander. Authorities have yet to confirm the letters’ authenticity or the existence of the group behind them.

The latest letters also distinguish between Pandits who never left the Valley — and are therefore “safe” — and those recruited under New Delhi’s rehabilitation program, who are accused of working for “masters” outside Kashmir.
The fresh threats have also triggered a political row.

Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) president and former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, called them a “conspiracy” aimed at delaying the restoration of statehood, which the region lost in 2019.
Abdullah also questioned why Hindu officers from outside the region were not facing similar threats.
His remarks drew sharp criticism from Kashmiri Pandit groups and the ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which accused him of being insensitive to the community’s fears.
Familiar fears
Government records show 44,167 Kashmiri migrant families registered as having left since 1990 citing security concerns, of which 39,782 were Hindu.
For Pandit community representatives, however, the latest threats are part of a much longer security problem.

Sanjay Tickoo, president of the Kashmiri Pandit Struggle Committee (KPSS), said the threats should be viewed against the backdrop of targeted killings and repeated security concerns faced by Pandit government employees in the Valley. He blames security lapses and says repeated meetings with officials since a wave of killings in 2022 have failed to resolve their concerns.
“Since 2022, meetings have resulted in nothing,” Tickoo told DW.
He also wondered how those making the threats have access to employees’ personal details.
“How are these details being posted on social media?” Tickoo asked.
Targeted killings have occurred sporadically in the years since. At least seven Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants during a spike in violence between 2020 and 2022.
One of the starkest cases was that of Rahul Bhat, a Pandit revenue official who was shot dead inside his government office in Budgam in May 2022.
The last confirmed targeted killing of a Kashmiri Pandit was in October 2022, when Puran Krishan Bhat, an orchard farmer, was shot dead in Shopian district.
Former Jammu and Kashmir police chief S P Vaid described the latest threats as part of a familiar militant playbook.
“There is nothing new in this,” Vaid told DW, calling it “a ploy by Pakistan to Islamize society.”
He said similar tactics had been used against migrant workers in the Valley.

The difference, this time, is the precision of the threats. Personal data that should not have been easily accessible has been made public, and no clear explanation of how it was leaked has been provided.
The return dilemma

The KPSS estimates roughly 6,500 Pandits who never left the Valley, along with another 4,000 who have returned as government employees under a federal rehabilitation scheme, live in India-administered Kashmir.
But the reintegration of those who fled decades ago has proved challenging.
Rahul Pandita, a journalist and author of “Our Moon Has Blood Clots: A Memoir of a Lost Home in Kashmir,” said the government’s record on rehabilitation was inadequate.

“The BJP has had no rehabilitation policy for Kashmiri Hindus,” Pandita told DW, arguing that the government employees in the Valley had returned under a policy introduced during the previous government of former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
Some land has been returned and cases of killings have been investigated, he said, but “it is too little and too late.”
Pandita said the bigger problem was that no government could guarantee a completely secure environment for a mass return.

“No matter what the government does, the situation will never be conducive enough for the Pandits to return,” he said, arguing that as long as Islamist militancy exists in the region, Kashmiri Hindus would still be targeted.
“It’s for them then to decide if they are willing to take such a risk,” he said.
Beyond government employees, some Pandits who have returned and established businesses in the Valley are already living there quietly, Pandita said.
“That is the best-case scenario for Kashmiri Pandits in Kashmir Valley,” he said.

blocks.caption: Pandits accuse the government in New Delhi of not doing enough to protect them from alleged Islamist threats Image: Firdous Nazir/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Security beyond protection
Sushobha Barve, executive secretary of the Center for Dialogue and Reconciliation, said the latest threats expose a wider security paradox.
“Despite claims of normalcy, a tiny group of active militants has successfully disrupted the lives of migrant families. Breaking the cycle of panic is essential,” Barve told DW.
She said there was also growing political frustration over the delay in restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood, arguing that this grievance cut across the region.

Amitabh Mattoo, an academic and professor of international relations at Jawaharlal Nehru University who has written extensively on Kashmir, said any return of Kashmiri Pandits had to be both secure and dignified.

“The state has an essential role in ensuring their physical security and in protecting their property, cultural and other legitimate rights. But security measures alone will not suffice,” Mattoo told DW.
“A sustainable return will also require patient reconciliation, engagement with local civil society, and the gradual rebuilding of inter-community trust and social and economic ties.” /dl

articles.title: AFP: China's Batanes claim part of coordinated malign influence campaign
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said the recent Chinese narrative claiming Batanes is part of a broader and coordinated foreign malign influence campaign.

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 2:59pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said the recent Chinese narrative claiming Batanes is part of a broader and coordinated foreign malign influence campaign.
At a press briefing, AFP spokesperson Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said the Batanes claim is synchronized with narratives involving Bajo de Masinloc and Ayungin Shoal.

“Let us not look at this as isolated incidents. These are all synchronized, persistent efforts of foreign malign influence to show to the public, first and foremost, and to the world that the AFP and the government have failed to secure and to protect our sovereignty and sovereign rights,” Trinidad said.
GMA News Online has sought comment from the Chinese Embassy in Manila about the matter but the office has yet to provide a statement as of posting time.
Trinidad said the narratives are designed to shape public perception and sow confusion. Such narratives came from “a group of academics from mainland China,” according to Trinidad.

He also said the AFP has observed deceptive messaging focusing on Batanes, Bajo de Masinloc, and Ayungin Shoal, alongside coercive and aggressive actions by Chinese military aircraft and the presence of Chinese research vessels.
The AFP spokesperson warned that such foreign malign influence activities have been increasing and could continue to escalate through 2028.
Trinidad said the Philippines should continue responding to every false narrative.
He added these Chinese activities have not weakened the AFP's resolve to continue its patrols and other operations in the disputed areas.

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual ship-borne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago including Luzon Sea and the waters around, within and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. — BAP, GMA News

The isolated village of al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, has been increasingly surrounded by Jewish settler outposts, and regularly blocked by Israeli forces who frequently operate an ad-hoc checkpoint at the entrance.

Six people, including three pupils at the school, have been killed in al-Mughayyir this year, in a surge of settler-related violence against Palestinians. One of them, 14-year-old Aws al-Naasan, was shot dead by a settler outside the school gates in April.

All Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. Many of the small ad-hoc settler outposts that have mushroomed around al-Mughayyir are illegal under Israeli law too.

articles.title: AFP: Chinese fighter jet intercepted PH patrol aircraft over Bajo de Masinloc
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday confirmed that Chinese fighter aircraft intercepted Philippine government aircraft conducting maritime patrols over Bajo de Masinloc.

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 2:57pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday confirmed that Chinese fighter aircraft intercepted Philippine government aircraft conducting maritime patrols over Bajo de Masinloc.
AFP spokesperson Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said a Chinese J-10 fighter intercepted Philippine aircraft during regular maritime air patrols over the disputed feature on September 2.

“Regular maritime air patrol domain awareness flights were conducted over Bajo de Masinloc. They were intercepted by fighter aircraft from the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force or the PLA Navy,” Trinidad said at a press briefing.
“On one instance, the crosshairs of the fighter aircraft had our aircraft on it,” he added.
Trinidad said the incident was among the actions China was using to demonstrate control over the area and weaken the Philippines’ resolve to continue its patrols.
Rather than deter the Philippines, however, Trinidad said such actions had strengthened the AFP’s determination to continue performing its mandate.
“Our resolve to keep performing our mandate has never been stronger,” Trinidad said.
He said the Philippines would continue working with its ally, the United States, as well as other like-minded countries such as Japan and Australia to support international law in the region.
GMA News Online has reached out to the Chinese Embassy in Manila and will update this story once a response is received.
Bajo de Masinloc is located 124 nautical miles off Masinloc, Zambales, and is within the Philippines’ 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost the entire South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion in annual shipborne commerce, including areas claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
The Philippines has referred to parts of the South China Sea within its maritime jurisdiction as the West Philippine Sea to reinforce its claims in the area.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.

In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines in its case against China, saying Beijing’s claims to historic rights over areas within the Philippines’ EEZ had “no legal basis.”
China has refused to recognize the ruling.— MCG, GMA News

MANILA, Philippines – Amid the ongoing Senate budget deliberations and the passage of the upper chamber’s legislative agenda, the Senate impeachment court on Tuesday, September 8, issued a new schedule for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Senators earlier agreed on adjustments in their work schedule primarily to achieve two goals: complete deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget on time and finish the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before the end of the year.

They also agreed to suspend the Senate rules and allow the finance committee to hold budget hearings while the plenary session is ongoing. Under this, senators who are in budget hearings during the plenary session will still be marked present during the roll call.
Impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero announced the latest calendar for the trial as follows:
September 8 to 30

items: 10 am to 2:30 pm: Impeachment trial
3 pm onwards: Plenary sessions, budget hearings, and committee hearings for the legislative agenda

items: No trial to give way to budget deliberations and preparation of Senate version of the proposed 2027 budget.

blocks.text: November 18

items: Trial resumes at 10 am to 2:30 pm (but may also be held earlier than November 18)

blocks.text: November 23

items: 10 am to 2:30 pm: Impeachment trial
3 pm onwards: Plenary sessions, budget hearings, and committee hearings for the legislative agenda

blocks.text: The senators earlier held a caucus on September 3, the same day that Senator Migz Zubiri raised the need for senators to agree on a work schedule adjustments that would allow them to allot time for budget deliberations alongside the impeachment trial and their normal work.

Zubiri said that without this schedule, it would not be possible for the Senate to finish deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget on time. It was also during his September 3 manifestation when he made a viral remark about the 12-hour workday of senators since the trial began, as sessions were being held after the trial ends in the afternoon.

“Sa totoo lang, Mr. President, pagod na pagod na ako. Twelve hours per day po tayo na nandito. From 9-9 nandito tayo,” he said, a remark that drew backlash online, with some netizens saying they, too, were tired from the grueling and low-wage realities faced by ordinary Filipino workers.
(Truth be told, Mr. President, I am very tired. We’re here 12 hours per day, from 9 am to 9 pm.)
In response to criticism of his remark, Zubiri later told reporters that he was just being “candid” and “honest.”

“Binanggit ko lang ang aking present condition at that time kasi napakahirap i-juggle ng tatlong napakalahagaang activities in Senate. It’s the first time na nangyari na nagkaroon ng impeachment, budget hearings, at legislative agenda,” he added.

(I just described my present condition at that time because it’s so difficult to juggle three important activities at the Senate. It’s the first time that we were holding the impeachment, budget hearings, and hearings for the legislative agenda simultaneously.)

The Senate is currently handling three major tasks: deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, the ongoing impeachment trial of Duterte, and the passage of its legislative agenda. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Elversberg: Bundesliga newcomers from tiny town make waves
articles.summary: A team from a small southwestern German town of just 7,000 inhabitants made history by sealing promotion to become the 59th club to play in the Bundesliga. Elversberg has got off to a memorable start.

image.caption: Elversberg have got off to a dream Bundesliga start, with two wins from twoImage: Thilo Schmuelgen/REUTERS

blocks.text: How are Elversberg doing in the Bundesliga?

So far, remarkably well. The smallest town ever to be represented in the top flight got off to a dream start on the Bundesliga's opening weekend, racing in to a 3-0 lead against 2024 champions Bayer Leverkusen. In the end, they held off a late surge to claim a 3-2 victory.

A trip to Borussia Mönchegladbach on matchday two looked to have brought them back down to earth, with the hosts leading 3-1 with little over 30 minutes to play. But a sensational comeback was crowned by a Maurice Krattenmacher winner in injury time. The win moved Elversberg above champions Bayern Munich as one of only four sides to have won both their opening two matches, but Krattenmacher was trying to keep some perspective.
"We know every opponent is good in the Bundesliga, but Bayern is on another level entirely. We’ll have to play as a team, and then we’ll see how it goes," he said.
Where is Elversberg?
Elversberg is a small town northeast of Saarbrücken in the small state of Saarland, in southwestern Germany.
As part of Spiesen-Elversberg, the town has a population of around 13,000 but Elversberg alone has just 7,000 people living in it. There is no train station and just three bakeries.
What is Elversberg's back story?
The club was formed in 1907, although folded during World War I before reforming in 1918.

In 2013, the club reached the third division alongside RB Leipzig, but they were promptly relegated. After two playoff defeats in 2016 and 2017, the club finally returned to the third division in 2022 and slowly began to gain a greater reputation.
The club's surge coincided with the appointment of Nils-Ole Book in 2017 and head coach Horst Steffen, a former Bundesliga player, a year later.

Book first joined as a scout before becoming sporting director, where he played a key role in recruitment. Steffen secured back-to-back promotions for the club as they reached the second division in 2023 as a newly-promoted side in the third division.

Germany and Newcastle striker Nick Woltemade played a key role in the club's promotion that year before moving on, and Bayern Munich's Paul Wanner enjoyed a successful loan spell at the club a year later.

In just their second season in the second division (2024-25), Elversberg were in the promotion playoff. But a 95th minute winner from Heidenheim broke their hearts, as they missed out on the top flight. Steffen left for Werder Bremen, star player Fisnik Asllani returned to Hoffenheim and five other key players departed. Not only did it look like the chance had gone, but the club looked more likely to battle against relegation the following season.
How did Elversberg reach the Bundesliga?

Aided by continuity at leading levels of the club, Elversberg found a way to turn a desperate situation into a remarkable one. What proved particularly helpful was having the father-son duo of Frank Holzer, chairman of the supervisory board, and Dominik, the president, leading the way and also calling the shots at main sponsor Ursapharm.

The appointment of head coach Vincent Wagner from Hoffenheim's reserve team was understated, but Wagner did not change much from Steffen's approach. Aided by former Bundesliga legend Mike Frantz, the assistant coach, and team manager Selina Wagner, who won a Champions League with Wolfsburg, the unit off the field appeared as united as the one forming on it.

The departure of star striker Younes Ebnoutalib to Frankfurt during the transfer window and sporting director Book to Borussia Dortmund in March didn't derail the club's promotion ambitions. After losing to relegation battlers Fortuna Düsseldorf in the penultimate game of the season, promotion hopes were wobbling once again. But a win on the final day was enough to keep their spot in second thanks to a superior goal difference. The Bundesliga had been reached.
"A friend of mine told me this week: 'If Elversberg get promoted, then it's like flying to the moon.' Well, today we made it to the moon," Wagner said afterwards.

blocks.caption: Two of the key figures in Elversberg's rise are former head coach Horst Steffen (left) and former sporting director Nils-Ole Book (right)Image: Steven Mohr/Jan Huebner/IMAGO

blocks.text: Where do Elversberg play?

At the Waldstadion an der Kaiserlinde, which has a capacity of 10,000 — more than the population of the town. Construction to reach Bundesliga requirements —15,000 capacity — is reportedly not expected to be finished until 2027, though Elversberg have already been granted an exemption to that rule.
Who are the key figures at Elversberg?
The strength of this team appears to be the collective, and the continuity in leadership positions, rather than one or two individuals.

On the field though, Bambase Conte was signed on loan from Hoffenheim and the attacking midfielder was integral to the club's promotion push. Long-standing goalkeeper Nicolas Kristof enjoyed a strong campaign, as did winger Lukas Petkov who pitched in with 13 goals and seven assists. Striker David Mokwa was bought in January for just €1.5 million, but aided the team down the stretch last term before scoring in the club's first two Bundesliga games.

The squad's average age is 25.3, making it one of the younger squads in the second division. Having reportedly made €10 million from transfers and spent just €3 million on new arrivals, it's clear what this team's approach is. But this summer, it will be intriguing to see how the club approaches the transfer market as it looks to build a squad capable of staying in the Bundesliga.
This article was updated on September 9, 2026 to reflect Elversberg's strong start to the new Bundesliga season.

articles.title: Female footballers offered egg freezing but doubts remain
articles.summary: Spain's football federation are set to join a handful of clubs in paying for female players to freeze their eggs during their careers. While players have pushed for the move, there are welfare…

image.caption: Alexia Putellas was reportedly a key figure in urging the Spanish FA to pay for egg freezingImage: Action Foto Sport/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Balancing motherhood and work is a challenge in any profession. But for footballers, whose peak sporting years coincide with their peak fertility, the choice can feel stark.

"For a woman whose sports career might last, say, 10 years at a high level, she starts thinking that getting pregnant really isn't an option," former Real Sociedad player, Larraitz Lucas, told DW. "When you are competing at a high level, all you are focusing on is the present."

Until the last few years, only about 2% of footballers got pregnant during their careers, with many leaving the sport to pursue motherhood. But with increasing professionalization, organizations are starting to wrestle with the question of how to deal with players who want to have children.

Binding maternity regulations were introduced to the sport only in 2021 and strengthened in 2024. But for those who wish to postpone their pregnancy while playing, the issue of freezing eggs as a fertility treatment has come to the fore.

US club, Racing Louisville, were the first club side to offer to pay for such treatments in 2021, while English club Chelsea have announced this month that egg freezing will be funded for any player that wants it.

But, perhaps more significantly, the Spanish football federation, RFEF, are expected to become the first national federation to announce a similar policy soon after reported lobbying from star player Alexia Putellas and others.
Playing during egg extraction a tough ask

Such options weren't available to Spaniard Lucas in her playing career, which ended more than a decade ago. While she went through egg retrieval, in her case it was so her partner could have an embryo implanted to carry the baby.

"You keep competing as best you can but no matter how much you try to align it with a weekend break from matches it's tough. Really, before, during, and after the egg extraction, well... it wasn't ideal," said Lucas.

Though it depends somewhat on circumstances, egg freezing can take around three weeks. Women inject themselves every day before their eggs are harvested and frozen under sedation. To use the eggs at a later date, they must be thawed and injected with sperm to create embryos.
IVF explained: Process, costs & risks

But, as athlete gynaecologist, Lamia Zafrani, told DW, egg freezing is far from straightforward. "Egg freezing is not an insurance policy that is guaranteed to pay out. It's always better if you freeze your eggs whilst you're young because you've got younger eggs to then use for future IVF.

"But actually there's no guarantee that when you defrost or thaw those eggs, turn them into embryos, that they'll actually be successful and result in a successful live birth. And I think it's these conversations that the athletes need to be made aware of because, at the end of the day, it's all about informed consent."
Egg freezing 'shouldn't be tool to pressure players'

Zafrani added that the number of athletes in her London clinic asking about the procedure has risen sharply in recent times. "It is definitely something that athletes are very much asking for," she said.

"But there's always nuance to all of these conversations. While it's great because the federations are listening to the players, ethically, it always does bring up the question of whether by offering egg freezing and fertility preservation, the underlying message is that you're telling your players 'don't get pregnant whilst you're working for us.' And that can be problematic."

It's a concern that is shared by Alexandra Gómez Bruinewoud. The legal director of global players' union, FIFPRO, was a co-author of the maternity policies adopted by football's global governing body, FIFA. She said FIFPRO have been working on policies for assisted reproduction, including the freezing of eggs, but that ensuring players were educated about their choices was paramount.

"We don't want it [egg freezing] to be used as a tool to pressure players not to become pregnant while they are playing because they are and they should always be fully entitled to decide when and how to become pregnant," Bruinewoud told DW.

blocks.caption: Former Germany goalkeeper Almuth Schult is one of relatively few players to give birth mid-careerImage: Memmler/Eibner-Pressefoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: There are, she said, several other considerations with regards to fertility and football, including doping concerns.

"When players go through assistive reproduction in general and if they are going to freeze eggs, in some situations they have to take hormones. And these substances can be prohibited in the WADA (World Anti Doping Agency) code.
"So we want to be sure to prevent a player being sanctioned when they are actually only trying to become pregnant or prepare things to be able to become pregnant in the future," said Bruinewoud.
Universal solution difficult to find

She added that with costs, recovery and procedures varying, mandating one blanket global rule would be near impossible, and should be guided by medical practitioners. It is also tough to apply any universal standard to a sport where professionalization and finance varies significantly between countries.

"In my view, the best solution for that is collective negotiation at national level,” Bruinewoud said. "These are very expensive procedures and most of the players worldwide will probably not have access to this because of the cost."

For all three women, the most important factors are choice, education and empowerment to get pregnant at a time that suits them. The hope is that, if managed well, egg freezing provides another option, rather than the default path.

articles.title: NCDA budget cut to P91M from from P187M in 2027
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA), an attached agency to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), is facing a budget cut from P187 million in 2026 to a proposed P91…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 2:39pm

The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA), an attached agency to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), is facing a budget cut from P187 million in 2026 to a proposed P91 million next year.

During the House briefing on DSWD's proposed budget of P241.2 billion for 2027, Akbayan Party-list Perci Cendaña noted that NCDA's latest proposed funding translates to P32 per person with disability (PWD).

"According to the NCDA, there are 2.8 million Filipinos registered as PWDs. Kaya nakapagtataka po na nangalahati ang budget ng NCDA, from P187 million in the 2026 in GAA to a mere P91 million in the 2027 NEP. If we are going to do the math, that's only P32 per PWD," he said.

(According to the NCDA, there are 2.8 million Filipinos registered as PWDs. That is why it's puzzling that the NCDA's budget was halved, from P187 million in the 2026 GAA to a mere P91 million in the 2027 NEP. If we are going to do the math, that's only P32 per PWD.)
But DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian assured that services remain in place for PWDs courtesy of the mother agency.

"Siyempre gusto namin na sana maibalik yung nawalang budget sa NCDA. Pero gusto ko lang linawin na hindi naman ibig sabihin na nabawasan ang tulong at suporta ng pamahalaan sa mga may kapansanan. Sa katunayan, malaking bahagi ng budget ng mother department itself goes through financial assistance through the AICS program for people with disability," he said.

(Of course, we wish that the missing budget for the NCDA could be restored. But I just want to clarify that this does not mean government assistance and support for persons with disabilities has been reduced. In fact, a large portion of the mother department's budget itself goes to financial assistance through the AICS program for people with disabilities.)

The DSWD explained that the lower budget for NCDA and other attached agencies was due to the lack of capital expenditure and the slashed allocation for maintenance and other operating expenses for next year.
The department added that the proposed NCDA budget for 2027 was supposedly over P200 million.

"Itong nawalang budget na ito ay capital expenditure. Nakalagay 'yan sa libro ng NCDA, to provide IT equipment to different PDAO offices. Kasi alam natin na may mga PDAO offices na maliit ang LGU at walang kapasidad na bumili ng mga gamit. So ayun ho yung nawalang suporta dahil non-recurring siya," said Gatchalian.

(This missing budget was for capital expenditure. It was in the NCDA's books to provide IT equipment to different PDAO offices. Because we know that there are PDAO offices where the LGU is small and lacks the capacity to purchase equipment. So that was the support that was removed because it is non-recurring.)
The lawmaker, on the other hand, expressed interest to increase the budget for NCDA for next year.
"At the proper time, Akbayan will move to restore the budget of the NCDA, at least to its 2026 levels," said Cendaña. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Sandiganbayan sets hearing on Martin Romualdez's bid for hospital arrest on Sept. 10
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan has set a court hearing on Thursday, September 10, to determine if there is a need for former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez to remain…

blocks.text: Published September 8, 2026 2:33pm

The Sandiganbayan has set a court hearing on Thursday, September 10, to determine if there is a need for former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez to remain under hospital arrest.

The anti-graft court issued the order for the said hearing a day after Ombudsman prosecutors filed a P7.4 billion plunder charge against Romualdez, former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio (personal assistant of Romualdez) and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra (president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation) over allegedly benefitting from a kickback scheme involving the government’s flood control projects.

Within the same day of the filing of the plunder case, the Sandiganbayan Third Division issued a warrant of arrest against Romualdez, later served to him by the police at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center where the lawmaker is currently confined.

“It be emphasized that the custody of accused Romualdez belongs to the court. If there are concerns regarding the accused's medical condition, it is only this court that can determine whether such condition affects the implementation of the warrant, the confinement of the accused at a hospital, or his commitment to a jail facility. Considering the allegations in accused Romualdez's Manifestation and Urgent Motion which raise serious concerns on his medical condition, the court deems it proper to set the Manifestation and Urgent Motion for hearing on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning,” the Sandiganbayan said.

“The Clerk of Court is directed to issue subpoena ad testificandum to Dr. Rody Sy, Dr. Rogelio Libarres, Dr. Kurt Allen V. Sibayan, and Dr. Rosalio P. Torres of Cardinal for the hearing on September 10, 2026, and to furnish PNP CIDG-NCR, as well as the foregoing doctors copies of this Order,” the anti-graft court added, referring to the Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detention Group National Capital Region.
In his Manifestation and Urgent Motion for hospital detention, Romualdez said he is currently confined at Cardinal due to the following diseases:
hypertensive atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease;

items: unstable angina;
coronary artery disease;
s/p pci (post percutaneous coronary intervention);
cerebrovascular ischemic disease;
type 2 diabetes mellitus;
hypertension;
dyslipidemia; and
primary hypothyroidism.

blocks.text: In the same September 8 ruling, the Sandiganbayan ordered Romualdez’s doctors to submit all results of pertinent medical examinations of the lawmaker to the anti-graft court.
Romualdez, on the other hand, was also ordered by the court to appear before the Sandiganbayan “should his [health] condition permit.”
Romualdez, cousin of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr., has maintained that he is innocent of all charges and that he will face his charges. —KG, GMA News

blocks.text: Here are the latest headlines from across Germany on Tuesday, September 8:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google.
September 8, 2026
Storage association warns Germany's gas reserves are dangerously low

Germany's gas and hydrogen storage association INES (Initiative for Energy Storage) on Tuesday said the country's gas storage facilities are at historically low levels as summer heat fades and winter approaches.
In a paper presented in Berlin, INES said reserves were at 53% of capacity as of early September, the lowest they have been at this point in time over the past 15 years.
The lobby group said levels could be brought up to 77% by November but only if input is dramatically increased.

INES said 77% capacity would be enough to cover consumer and industry needs if winter temperatures remain normal but added, "77% capacity will not be enough in the event of extremely cold temperatures."

With profit margins minimized by the wars in Russia and Iran, traders have little financial incentive to store natural gas according to INES. Storage facility operators are therefore calling on the German government to lower storage fees.

The Federal Ministry of Economy on the other hand, sees no reason for panic, adding that new LNG terminals off the German coast and pipeline deliveries from Norway can easily cover any potential shortages.

articles.title: Sept. 23: Senate may say number of votes to convict or acquit Duterte
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — With the help of the amici curiae, or “friends of the court,” Senate is expected to vote on Sept. 23 on whether to retain the 24-member voting base for the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — With the help of the amici curiae, or “friends of the court,” Senate is expected to vote on Sept. 23 on whether to retain the 24-member voting base for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
This came as Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo on Tuesday raised concerns over senators who may be unable to physically participate in the final vote on whether to convict or acquit Duterte.
According to presiding officer and Senator-judge Francis “Chiz” Escudero, “Tentatively, we will be setting the amici curiae on September 16 and the oral arguments of the parties on September 23.”
“Barring any unforeseen and/or questions of availability on the part of the amici curiae, hopefully, we will be able to do this in a week’s time,” he told Tulfo.

The presiding officer also said the Senate will not immediately resolve the matter through the usual ayes-and-nays procedure for questions involving rulings of the court, citing the “sensitive and serious nature” of the issue.
Instead, the court will seek the opinions and assistance of amici curiae, or individuals invited to provide independent expertise or perspective, to help the court resolve a legal issue.
There will be no impeachment trial on Sept. 16 as the Senate will hear the amici curiae on the voting threshold.
Afterwards, the prosecution and defense will be given 15 minutes each to present their positions during oral arguments on Sept. 23, after which the Senate will vote on the matter.
Choosing the amici curiae

Following a question from Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian to further clarify for the general public what the amici curiae is, Escudero explained that this refers to retired justices to guide the court on deciding on the matter.

“I hope that, through their extensive knowledge of the Constitution, as well as their experience in legal matters, they can provide us with their insights on this issue, whether in favor of or against either side,” the presiding officer said.

Senator-judge Kiko Pangilinan further explained, these amici curiae may include eminent legal experts, retired chief justice, retired supreme court justice, and experts in constitutional law and the like.
Pangilinan likewise made a motion for his colleagues to authorize Escudero to select these guests.

Escudero then reaffirmed that such consultations will be made. He said, during the break, that he has consulted both the prosecution and defense teams, and has come up with names agreed upon by both parties.

However, the court has yet to reveal the names of these amici curiae, saying they have yet to get in touch with these people, and ask whether they are willing or available to join the hearing on Sept. 16.
Whose vote are we counting?

This development came as Tulfo also on Tuesday moved for the Senate to revisit Escudero’s previous ruling that 16 votes are needed to convict the vice president, based on the two-thirds concurrence of the 24-member voting base.
Noting that four senators are currently unable to attend the trial, Tulfo asked, “My question now is very basic: When we refer to all members, who exactly are we counting?”
In addition, he asked whether the senators’ inability to attend the trial will automatically translate to a “no” vote.
He urged the Senate to resolve the matter “sooner than later” as the impeachment proceedings have been expedited, and the final question can come earlier than expected.
Tulfo warned that if the Senate insists on a fixed 24-member voting base, despite senators being unable to participate, their absence can result in what he called an “acquittal by default.”
He cited the Senate’s reliance on Avelino v. Cuenco, which, he said, considers only members within the coercive jurisdiction of the Senate in determining the voting base and existence of a quorum.
Meanwhile, Senator-judge Pia Cayetano said Tulfo’s statement that the Senate relies on Avelino v. Cuenco was “not accurate.”
“This body did not agree to that. The now-minority does not agree to that. So, I just want to put that on the record clearly,” Cayetano said.
“There are many ways to interpret Supreme Court decisions, but let’s not make it appear that it is jurisprudence or it is the rule in the Senate,” she told fellow senator-judges.

Senator-judge Robin Padilla, for his part, called on his peers to uphold their oath, maintaining that any amendments to the Constitution should go through the Senate Committee on Constitutional Amendments.
“The Constitution cannot be altered or circumvented,” Padilla noted.
Escudero then clarified if it was, indeed, Tulfo’s motion to appeal or reconsider the initial threshold ruling made on July 6.
According to Tulfo, he was asking whether the senators unable to be physically present in trial will also be allowed to vote.
“Let’s not forget, Mr. Presiding Officer, that these people are still members of the Senate,” Tulfo said.
Cayetano, who again rose to make a manifestation, said before setting the date, the Senate should first ask if it even has the right to decide on it.

The senator cited Escudero’s July 6 ruling on the matter and said, “Your ruling, Mr. Presiding Officer, was made. Your ruling was if there’s anyone who questions it, then the recourse is to go to the Supreme Court.”
However, Escudero replied that based on Tulfo’s manifestation, aside from identifying the base figure, Tulfo wants it decided by the impeachment court.
Pangilinan and Cayetano likewise raised before the court that there exists a plea from their detained colleagues, Sens. Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada, to allow them to attend Duterte’s trial.
Escudero said that matter was previously referred to the Senate as a legislative body, not to the impeachment court.
Sen. Raffy Tulfo, meanwhile, asked how the absent senators would be able to vote intelligently if they were not able to attend the proceedings.
As of now, Sens. Marcoleta, Estrada, Loren Legarda and Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa have been unable to attend the trial.
Legarda has been out of the country and on extended medical leave. This came at a time when the Office of the Ombudsman announced that she is under preliminary investigation for a plunder complaint.
Dela Rosa, on the other hand, is in hiding over an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court. /apl

articles.title: Flights resume gradually in Indonesia after volcanic eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA — Indonesia had planes flying again on Tuesday after a volcanic eruption forced the country’s major airports to close for days, with authorities saying that flights would resume…

blocks.text: JAKARTA — Indonesia had planes flying again on Tuesday after a volcanic eruption forced the country’s major airports to close for days, with authorities saying that flights would resume gradually.
The disruption, caused by the eruption of Anak Krakatau, halted nearly 3,000 flights and stranded more than 340,000 passengers.
The country’s main airport serving the capital Jakarta and four other airports reopened early Tuesday after authorities cleared volcanic ash from critical infrastructure.
Transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi told reporters it would take time for flight schedules to return to normal.
Dudy said there were around 178 aircraft at Soekarno–Hatta International Airport, Jakarta’s main air travel hub.
“We will be operating these aircraft, but before we do so, we want to ensure their airworthiness. So, it may take a bit of extra time,” he said.
“We ask for a little patience from passengers and the public, as we will be carrying out inspections to ensure that these aircraft are fit to fly,” he added.
The transport minister said three flights departed shortly after the airport reopened, including two commercial flights to eastern Indonesia.
Airport operator Angkasa Pura Indonesia said in a statement that volcanic ash had been cleared from the runway and other areas to ensure the facilities were safe for flights.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano erupted at least three times on Tuesday morning alone, according to the head of the Geology Agency, Lana Saria.
It has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea nearly a century ago in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed more than 400 people and displaced thousands. /dl

blocks.text: PARIS — The Eiffel Tower was set to reopen Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group which later apologized.

The operating company that runs the Paris landmark, SETE, acknowledged that the Hindu delegation had requested the visit be organised so as to limit “interactions with women” and said that “these conditions should not have been accepted”.
It said the landmark was due to reopen on Tuesday following a meeting the previous day between staff and management.
The Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) spiritual movement apologized for “any pain or inconvenience caused” by the incident.
“To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower,” the organization wrote on X.
“Due to the size of our delegation, the visit was arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal operating hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others.”

Eiffel Tower staff said in a statement that it condemned “professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex” during the visit by the delegation.

“Instructions were given to female employees of the Eiffel Tower and to female employees of contractors to make themselves invisible in order to welcome this delegation,” the staff said in their statement, adding they were shocked to have been put in such a situation.

“Some were asked to leave their posts and withdraw to other areas. In some posts they were replaced by men. And all female employees were instructed not to go through or cross certain areas while the delegation was present.” /dl
