articles.title: Ebola: Why children are last to be treated in medical crises
articles.summary: The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been devastating. Since the outbreak began in mid-May, more than 3,000 people have died. Almost half of people infected with Ebola…

blocks.text: The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been devastating. Since the outbreak began in mid-May, more than 3,000 people have died.

Almost half of people infected with Ebola are expected to die, and the mortality rate is particularly high for young children. According to a commentary by Doctors Without Borders recently published in medical journal The Lancet, the mortality rate for children under the age of 5 is over 60%.
But often, it’s because of a lack of medication and information on how to use it with young patients, rather than then disease itself.
“Children must be centered in Ebola treatment and prevention research,” the aid organization wrote in early September.

At the heart of the debate is the EBO-PEP study, which began mid-July. The study looks at an experimental antiviral drug called obeldesivir, which is being studied for its ability to protect people exposed to the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, the strain responsible for the current deadly outbreak.

But children weighing less than 30 kilograms (about 66 pounds) and around 12 years old or younger, were not included in the original study. But that could change soon with protocols to include children weighing over 20 kilograms.

Children weighing less than 20 kilograms — that is, roughly 6 years old or younger — won’t be included in the treatment. There is an alternative treatment for them: Another antiviral drug, remdesivir, given intravenously. But as Doctors Without Borders argued, a 10-day course of infusions is difficult to administer during an outbreak, especially for young children.

According to Neal Russell, a pediatric doctor based in London who consults for Doctors Without Borders and who was also the lead author of the Lancet commentary, young children are at particularly high risk from Ebola. This could be due to their weakened immune systems, underlying health conditions, or the fact that treating them for Ebola is especially challenging in an outbreak.

For example, children are often harder to diagnose than adults because early symptoms resemble other illnesses, and young children often find it difficult to describe their symptoms accurately. Other issues include the fact that children cannot always be accompanied into an Ebola treatment center by their parents or caregivers, something that is especially important in their recovery. Younger Ebola patients also require closer monitoring and specially trained staff.
Ebola in Berlin

In May, an American doctor was treated at Berlin’s Charite hospital after contracting the Bundibugyo Ebola virus while caring for patients. His wife and their four children were also considered at high risk. The medical team in Germany decided to treat the family prophylactically with an experimental antibody drug called MBP134.
“Of course, a careful risk benefit assessment had to be carried out,” said Han Ngoc Le, a doctor at the hospital who was involved in the treatments.
The available data about the drug’s impact on children was very limited. But at the same time, the children were at high risk of catching Ebola after close contact with their sick father.

In the end, all the family remained healthy and no apparent side effects were seen. It’s unclear whether the experimental treatment prevented infection in the children. Such a small sample can’t be mapped onto the larger population either.

But the test was valuable nonetheless. “The mere fact that the antibody was so well tolerated even in 1-year-olds and children under 12 is a valuable finding upon which future studies can build,” Le said.
Why do such gaps in knowledge exist?
Le explained that, from a medical perspective, children cannot simply be thought of as “small adults.”

Their metabolisms function differently, they react differently to medications, their pharmacokinetics — what a body does with a drug — are simply different. The same sort of cautions also apply to pregnant women.

That’s why dosages of medication can’t simply be transferred from adults to children. It’s also why any new medications require separate studies so that specific dosages can be determined and potentially special formulations can be developed. Children might require kid-friendly syrups instead of adult-size tablets, for example.

“All of this creates extra costs,” said Marc Biot, access coordinator for Europe at Doctors Without Borders, who works to ensure people in need can get affordable, good-quality medical products. He said research institutions and pharmaceutical companies often see investing extra in pediatric studies as a lower priority.

“It is faster and it can be cheaper if you only focus on adults,” said Biot — which is why treating children and pregnant women usually only becomes part of the research at a later stage of drug development. “That is our plea — a plea not only to the scientists, to the pharmaceutical companies, but also to those who fund and allow trials to happen — to allow that to happen on the same speed for adults as for children and pregnant women.”
Biot said it’s sad to see that pressure is needed to make it happen. “Whenever you start a clinical trial, you also should include pregnant woman or children,” he argued.
A difficult balance

None of this is new. In 2020, the Global Accelerator for Pediatric Formulations network was founded — supported by the World Health Organization(WHO) — to accelerate the development and availability of child-friendly medicine worldwide.
This isn’t an issue limited to Ebola. Russell pointed to the 2024 mpox epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where children made up a large proportion of those infected or killed.

Although a vaccine existed for mpox, it wasn’t made for children. The WHO advised it be used “off label” for minors, but they tended to get it a lot later than adults anyway. Experts say they’ve observed similar patterns with other diseases including HIV, tuberculosis, and during the COVID-19 pandemic.

blocks.caption: When it comes to the development of medicines and vaccines, the first samples are often made for adult patients Image: Thomas Lohnes/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “When you’re doing a research study, which is not in an emergency, [it makes sense] to protect children and pregnant women from any potential harm of an investigational product,” said Russell. “But when you’re in an emergency, the balance between protecting those people from any potential harm from research, and protecting them from the very fatal disease, changes.”

Berlin-based doctor Le believes children and pregnant women should be considered right from the beginning of any new clinical trials. “They shouldn’t be excluded from participation just like that,” she said. “Instead, sub-studies or parallel studies should be set up from the outset.”

Russell calls for a similar approach. He wants to see all people benefit equally from scientific progress during a health crisis — especially in a health emergency, when the most vulnerable should not be the last to benefit from that progress.
“No matter who you are, you should have the same opportunity to have access to these medical products,” he said. /dl

articles.title: Five killed as Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport
articles.summary: Video footage from Miami shows an Amazon Air cargo plane overshoot the runway while attempting to land.

articles.title: New videos of man in 9/11 lawsuit reveal extremist links
articles.summary: The footage and other evidence the FBI failed to share undermine Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials.

blocks.text: The man at the heart of a $1 trillion (£733bn) lawsuit brought by 9/11 families had extensive links to Saudi government officials and went paintballing with one of al-Qaeda's future leaders, video obtained by the BBC reveals.
The footage, which the FBI had within days of the 2001 attacks, stands in stark contrast to Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials that he was an extremist and a Saudi spy.

Bayoumi, who claimed to be a student when he was in the United States, is seen in one clip embracing Anwar al-Awlaki, who would go on to lead al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula. In another, Bayoumi and Awlaki are paintballing near San Diego with an official from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs.
The videos form part of the 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia and have never been shown publicly before.

The lawsuit argues Saudi Arabia was complicit in the attacks and that Bayoumi aided two of the 19 hijackers who flew planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon - with another crashing in Pennsylvania.
Bayoumi was arrested in the UK by the Metropolitan Police days after the attacks and the videos were found among his possessions, along with other crucial evidence.
This included a diagram of a plane with a flight descent equation written alongside.

Multiple FBI agents received copies of the diagram, but it was never shared with the British interrogators, even though it had been couriered to the police station where Bayoumi was being held in custody.

The diagram was also kept from some FBI agents investigating Bayoumi, as well as from the 9/11 Commission - the independent inquiry into the largest mass murder in US history, in which nearly 3,000 people were killed. Bayoumi was never prosecuted.
He and the Saudi government did not respond to the BBC's requests for comment, but both have always denied any involvement in, or prior knowledge of, the attacks. The FBI declined to comment.

After a judge ruled the lawsuit could go ahead in 2018, thousands of documents, as well as videos and photographs, have been released to the court and also declassified through an executive order made by former President Joe Biden.

BBC Panorama and Radio 4 have examined these documents, and spoken to dozens of special agents and investigators, to trace the evidence the FBI gathered about Bayoumi and Saudi Arabia's alleged involvement in 9/11 - and to understand why it was never fully pursued over 25 years.
Our investigation also found:

items: The plane diagram was sent to the FBI's New York office and was analysed, according to an FBI source. But a US Department of Justice (DOJ) official told the BBC he was never shown a proposal to prosecute Bayoumi based on the evidence, even though "we've convicted people for less"
FBI agents in San Diego, where Bayoumi had lived in the US, repeatedly requested copies of evidence but never received most of it
The San Diego and Los Angeles FBI offices were both blocked from interviewing Bayoumi's Saudi government contacts

Staff on the 9/11 Commission objected to the conclusion that Bayoumi was "unlikely" to have been involved with extremists, prompting the report to attribute this to "our investigators who have dealt directly with him"

blocks.text: Omar al-Bayoumi arrived in San Diego from Saudi Arabia in 1994. He claimed to be studying English, but court records show that within a few years he had, in effect, abandoned his studies. He was more usually found organising religious events, often with a camcorder pressed to his eye.

One video Bayoumi filmed, from 1997 or early 1998, shows men, including Anwar al-Awlaki, paintballing. Filmed near San Diego, the group engages in urban combat scenes and target practice, many wearing military fatigues.

At one point, some of the men charge into battle, shouting "Allahu Akbar". A visiting Saudi sheikh is with the group and Bayoumi can also be heard addressing Anwar al-Awlaki with the honorific "Sheikh Anwar".

The following morning, in Birmingham, officers began the meticulous process of logging and bagging up evidence in his properties - a cache of many thousands of pages of documents, hundreds of photographs, flight ticket stubs, phone cards, and carrier bags and boxes containing at least 80 videotapes.

Within hours of the search starting, several items of documentary evidence - categorised as the highest priority at the direction of the FBI - were taken by police directly to Paddington Green, where the FBI had stationed an agent.

This evidence included a phone book containing more than two dozen names of Saudi government officials in the US and Saudi Arabia; flight simulator software; tickets and travel documents; and the yellow lined page of a notebook with the sketch of a plane, which an officer had marked: "contains handwritten notes mathematical calculations re height of planes".
Eighteen years later, the FBI would hand the notebook page to the court in the 9/11 families' lawsuit, following a subpoena. The page was made public in 2022.

"It's the mathematical calculation of the crash," Jodi Westbrook Flowers, a member of the 9/11 families' legal team, told the BBC. "When we figured out what it was, we knew that it was the smoking gun that we'd been looking for."

The equation, written in Omar al-Bayoumi's handwriting, indicates the height and distance required for a pilot to guide an aeroplane to a given object on the ground. Underneath it is a small drawing of a plane and a series of numbers.
Last year, the federal judge in the families' lawsuit found the notebook page, on the face of it, "connects Bayoumi with knowledge of the 9/11 Attacks".
In 2021, when questioned about it in court, Bayoumi said he had the diagram because he liked finding equations and could not remember when he had written it.

By the evening of 22 September 2001, copies of the plane diagram were in London in the hands of both the FBI and UK counter-terror police - and just metres from the custody suite where Omar al-Bayoumi was being questioned. Records show they passed through at least three further FBI agents in the following two days.

But here, the mystery begins. The FBI briefed the Met officers to question Bayoumi about the other high-priority exhibits, but the detectives in the custody suite were never given, or briefed about, the plane diagram.

Many FBI agents have told us the immediate aftermath of 9/11 was a round-the-clock frenzy. But it is hard to understand how a piece of evidence of this importance, in a case being handled with considerable urgency, was not put into the hands of the interviewing detectives.
The FBI declined to respond to our questions. The Metropolitan Police told us it could not comment because of the ongoing legal case.
On the day he would need to be charged or released, the Met detectives joined a conference call with several senior officials from the US Department of Justice and FBI.

Panorama and Radio 4 have spoken to two participants at the meeting. One recalls the British detectives setting out the evidence they believed met the threshold for the Americans to extradite Bayoumi to face charges in the US.
The response from the DOJ officials was that no extradition would be sought because there was insufficient evidence.
On 28 September 2001, Bayoumi was released.
But, at that point, the FBI had not shipped all of the evidence found in Birmingham back to the US, let alone exhaustively analysed it.
One memorandum from the FBI's legal attache in London, sent two weeks later, noted there were a "number of videos, floppy disks and documentation still to be viewed".
After Omar al-Bayoumi's release, agents continued analysing the evidence against him.
The BBC understands the plane diagram was couriered from London for analysis at the New York Field Office, which was in overall charge of the 9/11 investigation.

But we have not been able to trace any records of this analysis or its conclusions. A 2021 Presidential order required the FBI to declassify files relating to its 9/11 investigations, including into Bayoumi.

However, of the files released, the FBI has only produced one document referring to the diagram, despite its evidential significance, and this was only created 11 years after the diagram's initial discovery in 2001.
The diagram seems to have fallen into a black hole.
It was not passed on to San Diego, where Bayoumi had lived in the USA and where the FBI Field Office was also investigating him.

In fact, San Diego - where agents were interviewing his associates, searching his mosque, analysing his telephone records and bank statements - received almost none of the large volume of evidence seized by the Met Police in Birmingham.

Rick Lambert, who ran the FBI's investigation there, told the BBC his office made repeated requests to New York to send copies of all the evidence. "Their position was, we're in charge of the case; we'll send it to you when we're finished analysing."

Lambert said New York did not comply his office's requests. "I believe there is the potential that had we received that evidence and analysed it, that we would have been able to put the pieces of the puzzle together much more quickly."
Documents show that, in spring 2002, the San Diego office was ultimately able to get copies of a handful of videos by obtaining them not from New York, but from the FBI liaison in London.

Jeffrey Breinholt, then the deputy director of counter-terrorism at the Department of Justice who oversaw prosecutors working on terrorism charges after 9/11, told the BBC that Bayoumi's name had come up "as one of the hot possibilities for charges".

But he said the New York Attorney's Office never sent charges to him or his colleagues for approval. If they had, the plane diagram would have been significant evidence against Bayoumi, he said. "We've convicted people for less."
The paintballing video, Breinholt told us, is another "very telling bit of evidence" with the presence of Anwar al-Awlaki being "pretty damn significant".
"As a manager who reviewed a lot of proposed terrorism cases over the years, I can tell you that that would have jumped out. I think it would be a material support charge against Bayoumi."
There were no charges brought against Bayoumi.
Agents who tried to investigate Omar al-Bayoumi encountered other roadblocks.

In October 2001 in San Diego, Lambert and colleagues wanted to interview a number of Saudi officials in the US - many connected to the Ministry of Islamic Affairs - who they suspected had co-ordinated the help Bayoumi gave to two of the hijackers, Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar.
Because diplomats have a special protected status, the agents needed permission from FBI headquarters and the State Department.
"The answer came back, 'no, you're not going to do that'," Lambert, who is now a consultant for the 9/11 families in their lawsuit, told us.

Agents in Los Angeles experienced a similar outcome the following year, when they applied to interview a Saudi religious diplomat Bayoumi had met immediately after his first encounter with Hazmi and Mihdhar in the city.

"We hit a roadblock so hard, I think we all had airbag burns," said Steve Moore, who oversaw the FBI's 9/11 investigation in LA. Moore says his team made repeated requests to interview the official, but permission never came.
Like the FBI, the State Department declined to comment.

In October 2003, the 9/11 Commission - set up by Congress to provide a "full and complete" account of the attacks - interviewed Omar al-Bayoumi in Riyadh. He had returned to Saudi Arabia in the months after his release by British police.

The interview was conducted, in the presence of Saudi secret police, by the Commission's executive director Philip Zelikow, a former advisor to President George W Bush, along with a senior staffer and an agent from FBI headquarters.

The Commission's notes from the time record that Bayoumi was given a remarkable degree of reassurance during the interview. He "was told that no-one believes he knowingly helped the hijackers carry out their terrorist mission".

Bayoumi indignantly said he was a peace-lover who had become "a victim of the victims". During the interview, the delegation broke away for a multi-course dinner hosted by the Mabahith, the secret police, without Bayoumi.

After the interview concluded, the Mabahith told the American delegation they "would like to see him cleared". The Americans responded that no exoneration would be possible before their report was published.
When the 9/11 Commission Report was published in July 2004, Bayoumi was, in effect, cleared. It described him as "obliging and gregarious" and stated there was no evidence he had extremist views.
But some staff on the Commission were not convinced of Bayoumi's innocence, and thought it likely he knew Hazmi and Mihdhar were al Qaeda operatives.
The BBC can reveal that those staff objected to a line in the report concluding that he was "an unlikely candidate for clandestine involvement with Islamist extremists".
In the end, a compromise was agreed, and this conclusion was attributed to "our investigators who have dealt directly with him and studied his background".
The line was written based on the four and a half hours the Commission delegation had spent with Bayoumi, which included the interruption for dinner.
The Commission never saw the plane diagram, the paintballing video, written evidence of Bayoumi's alleged extremism, or much of the rest of the evidence the Met Police had seized.

Philip Zelikow did not answer the specific questions we asked him. He told the BBC the 9/11 Commission's findings had been subject to two government reviews, in 2015 and 2021, and the Commission had been "open about our suspicions and uncertainties. We were careful about whom to accuse of complicity in mass murder."
The Department of Justice told us it was unable to comment on matters and decisions from 25 years ago, involving staff who no longer worked there.
The head of the FBI's 9/11 investigation, Mary Galligan, has previously stated the Commission had "access to everything".

We tried to contact Omar al-Bayoumi through the Saudi government, but he did not respond. He has previously denied knowing Hazmi and Mihdhar were hijackers, that he was a Saudi spy, and that he had any involvement in 9/11.
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia did not respond to our request for comment. It has previously said any allegation that Saudi Arabia or its officials are complicit in 9/11 is categorically false.

articles.title: How an IT engineer used AI to aid Nepal’s flood response
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — When devastating floods struck Nepal on the morning of August 26, Niraj Bhusal was getting ready for a routine day at the Ministry of Finance. When news arrived that the Rasuwagadhi…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — When devastating floods struck Nepal on the morning of August 26, Niraj Bhusal was getting ready for a routine day at the Ministry of Finance.

When news arrived that the Rasuwagadhi customs office on the China-Nepal border had been swept away, Bhusal, like many Nepalis, was dumbfounded. Unified, reliable information about the unfolding crisis was scarce. Bhusal knew he had to act, and quickly. That was when he decided to put his training in ‘AI and governance’ to test. Bhusal, who is an IT engineer at the ministry, worked through the night and single-handedly developed an integrated, accessible, and AI-driven disaster response portal to track casualties, locate missing persons and coordinate government relief.

Bhusal recently gained access to ‘Grok Bot’—the AI model developed by Elon Musk’s xAI. He has programmed the model to build the entire layout, design, and JavaScript coding for a web application called the ‘Rasuwa-Bhote Koshi Flood’ portal. Hosted on GitHub, the portal automatically aggregates and structures information from diverse official sources, including the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, Nepal Police, Nepali Army, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), news outlets, press releases, and satellite APIs.

To ensure absolute accuracy and credibility, Bhusal implemented a strict validation system. “Once the code went live on GitHub, the AI began sending new updates to my mobile phone every five minutes,” Bhusal told Kantipur recently. “To prevent errors, I verify each update manually. That first night, my laptop never went idle, and I only managed to sleep at 4:00 am.”

blocks.caption: Initially launched in Nepali, the portal is now also available in English to help Nepalis living abroad and international organisations monitor the situation.  Post Photo

blocks.text: As the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers raged, tearing through roads, power plants, bridges, and settlements, the AI worked tirelessly in the background, scanning the internet for news on casualties, relief fund commitments, missing person requests, ongoing rescues and official government statements.
Initially launched in Nepali, the portal is now also available in English to help Nepalis living abroad and international organisations monitor the situation.

What began as a simple Google Form to collect details about missing persons has now evolved into a critical node in Nepal’s disaster response architecture. After the government launched its official rescue portal, Bhusal integrated his database with the NDRRMA’s system, routing citizens who visit his site directly to official state relief and rescue portals.

To map physical destruction, Bhusal integrated satellite imaging from Copernicus, the European Union’s Earth observation programme, allowing the website to show precise damage to houses, roads, and bridges. Copernicus recognised his efforts, mentioning him on the social media platform X.

Bhusal’s solo initiative has sparked an outpouring of unexpected global support to keep the portal running. Shristi Mainali, a Nepali residing in Australia, contributed $210 in server credits. At the same time, Tabor T., a community developer at SpaceX AI (Grok’s parent company), stepped in with an additional $100 to ensure the site remained active during traffic spikes. Five other supporters contributed $185 via the ‘Buy Me a Coffee’ platform.

This is not Bhusal’s first time on the front lines of a national crisis. In his 13-year career in public service, he has served as an IT officer at the Ministry of Urban Development, the Prime Minister’s Office, and the Ministry of Water Supply. During the devastating 2015 earthquake, he was stationed at Tribhuvan International Airport and customs, managing the complex logistics of international relief materials.
Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle has highly praised Bhusal’s initiative, actively sharing and retweeting the portal’s updates on social media.
Bhusal now plans to officially hand over the portal to the government, hoping the state will adopt it as a permanent model for emergency communications.
Bhusal says that as citizens, everybody should contribute whatever and however they can in times of crisis.
“The government does not have to do everything alone,” he said. “I designed this portal treating every single victim as a member of my own family.” /dl

articles.title: Water levels at San Roque Dam, Pangasinan rivers remain under close watch
articles.summary: PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level. As of 5 a.m.…

blocks.text: (Photo via Liezle Inigo)
PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level.
As of 5 a.m. on Sept. 7, the dam’s water level was at 279.79 meters above sea level (masl), with an inflow of 338 cubic meters per second (cms) and a combined outflow of 746 cms.
Two gates were opened at the dam. Gate No. 2A was opened to 1.0 meter, while Gate No. 2B was opened to 1.5 meters. The Low Level Outlet was also releasing 125 cms.
The elevated discharge comes as authorities continue to monitor river conditions downstream, particularly communities located near waterways and flood-prone areas.

At 6 a.m., the Marusay River in Calasiao was above the critical level, while the Sinucalan River in Sta. Barbara, Pantal River in Dagupan City, and Agno/Bañaga River in Bugallon were above normal levels.
The Camiling River in Camiling, Tarlac was at normal level. No level reading was indicated in the monitoring report for the Bued/Cayanga River in San Fabian and Balingcaguing River in Mabini.
Residents near rivers and low-lying communities are urged to remain alert, monitor advisories, and follow evacuation or other safety directives when issued.

articles.title: 'Takot yan?': VP Duterte doesn't talk, act like someone who is in fear, says Adiong
articles.summary: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.…

blocks.text: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.

This, as Adiong chided Duterte for playing the victim card after being issued an arrest warrant for three counts of grave threats, which stemmed from claims of planning to assassinate President Marcos and other members of the First Family.
The Vice President’s ordeal prompted her to declare over the weekend, "I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila [pulis] ako (I feel the police is out to kill me).
"I have documented threats and harrassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them," she also said.
But Adiong doesn't buy Duterte’s fearful facade one bit.
“Kung titignan niyo, hindi po ito yung taong takot (If you look at her, she does not appear to be someone who is afraid). Actually, in fact, it’s the other way around,” he said.

He also pointed to Duterte’s previous public statements that he said appeared to invoke violence against President Marcos, as well as her continued requests for travel clearance, as inconsistent with her claim that she had been under threat since 2023.

“Siya yung nagbibigay ng mga statement na nagpapahiwatig ng violence against the President, pupugutan ng ulo (She was the one making statements suggesting violence against the President, including that he would be beheaded)... So it’s not an indication of someone who’s been receiving threats,” he said.
These notwithstanding, Adiong stressed that any threat against Duterte should be taken seriously and properly investigated by authorities.
He said the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) had given her an opportunity to submit information about the threats she claimed to have received, but no such information had been provided.

“They were given the chance. They were called, invited by the NBI na isubmit po nila kung ano po yung threats na ... natatanggap nila (They were called and invited by the NBI to submit information about the threats they had received.
“Pero hanggang ngayon, wala po silang naibibigay (But until now, they have not provided anything)," Adiong noted.

Seemingly referring to Duterte’s subsequent criticisms on the court and police, the Mindanao congressman stressed that public officials should respect the courts and the law even when proceedings or their outcomes are unfavorable to them.

“In this case, whether or not favorable sa’yo, kailangan mo talaga as an elected official to prove to the people that we have our laws, we have to respect our laws, and only through our laws and through our courts can we defend ourselves."

(In this case, whether or not it is favorable to you, as an elected official you have to prove to the people that we have laws, that we have to respect them, and that only through our laws and courts can we defend ourselves.)
The law applies to everyone

For Adiong, the grave threats case demonstrates that the law applies equally to everyone regardless of status or position, rejecting claims from Duterte’s camp and supporters that the proceedings constitute political persecution.

“Ito pong nangyayari ngayon, ito po ang nagpapatunay na gumugulong po ang hustisya sa ating bansa. Wala pong tinitingnan na status or posisyon ng isang tao pagdating sa pananagutan at sa pag-implement ng mga patakaran o ating batas,” he said.

(What is happening now proves that justice is taking its course in our country. No one’s status or position is considered when it comes to accountability and the implementation of our rules and laws.)
He said the criminal case should also be distinguished from Duterte’s ongoing impeachment proceedings.
“Magkaiba naman po yung mga hukom na tumatayo dito at yung magiging verdict po ay magkaiba (The judges handling these cases are different, and the verdicts will also be different)."

articles.title: DSWD flags bogus UPLIFT aid for students
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood,…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Assistance.

The posts claim that the government is giving ₱2,000 to elementary students, ₱3,000 to junior high school students, ₱5,000 to senior high school students, and ₱8,000 to college students under the program.
DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said educational assistance is not part of UPLIFT.

“Paalala po natin sa ating mga kababayan na walang educational assistance sa ilalim po ng ating UPLIFT Assistance. Ito pong assistance na ito ay tulong maibsan ang epekto ng pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin (We remind our fellow Filipinos that there is no educational assistance under UPLIFT Assistance. This assistance is intended to help ease the impact of rising prices of goods),” Dumlao said.
The posts also direct users to registration links, which the DSWD said are unauthorized.
Dumlao said there is no need to register for UPLIFT because its beneficiaries have already been identified using the latest Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) data.

“Mangyaring huwag po i-click ang inyong mga makikitang link na nagsasabing maaari kayong magparehistro dahil scam po ito (Please do not click on links claiming that you can register because these are scams),” she added.
Qualified beneficiaries under Groups 2 and 3 of the UPLIFT program receive ₱2,000 per month until December.

UPLIFT Assistance is among the Marcos administration’s initiatives to help poor, near-poor, and low-income Filipinos cope with the economic impact of the energy emergency brought about by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
The public may verify information on UPLIFT Assistance and other DSWD programs through the Department’s official social media pages or the DSWD Online Grievance Portal.

articles.title: Alcantara, partner rule doubles tilt in Thailand
articles.summary: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.

blocks.text: (Francis Casey Alcantara / Facebook / Impact )

Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.
Alcantara, 34, and Sornlaksup recovered from a second-set stumble and held their ground by protecting their 8-3 advantage to fend of their persistent Indian rivals.
“Thank you Pawit Sornlaksup for an incredible week and for carrying me through some tough matches!” Alcantara wrote on social media.
“It was a pleasure sharing the court with you bro! Special thanks to Coach Coach Carlo Core Tennis Academy BKK for always being there and helping me out again this week,” he added.
Prior to their title victory, Alcantara and Sornlaksup outlasted locals Thantub Suksumrarn and Tanapatt Nirundorn (7-5, 7-5) in the opening round.

They followed it up with a gritty 6-2, 4-6, 11-9 quarters victory over Japanese Shu Muto and Ko Suzuki to book their ticket to the semifinals, where they ultimately pulled off a 1-6, 6-4, 10-4 triumph against Americans Hugo Hashimoto and Michael Blando.
The tournament serves as a training ground for Alcantara, who will be competing in the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 late this month.

articles.title: Ely Buendia, Chito Miranda sell out Dubai concert amid Middle East tensions
articles.summary: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making…

blocks.text: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making concert planning a more complicated proposition.
And yet, some acts continue to defy the odds, demonstrating that music can be more than entertainment in uncertain times.
Ely Buendia and Chito Miranda were among those artists
The two brought OPM nostalgia to Dubai on Aug. 30, performing to a sold-out Coca-Cola Arena.
For the UAE’s Filipino community, the show also offered something beyond nostalgia: a chance to reconnect with home through live music at a time when the region remains unsettled.

Buendia, best known as the former frontman of Eraserheads, and Miranda, lead vocalist of Parokya ni Edgar, represent different eras of Philippine rock but share a deep connection with Filipino audiences.
The concert was presented by Tiana Entertainment Inc., headed by founder and CEO Bojie Yangco, who has worked in live entertainment for more than two decades.

The company has mounted Filipino concerts in markets including the U.S., Canada, Australia, the Middle East and Kazakhstan, with artists such as Rivermaya, SB19, Ben&Ben, Buendia and Miranda among its previous projects.

articles.title: Palace respects Ombudsman filing of plunder case vs Romualdez
articles.summary: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the…

blocks.text: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the flood control scandal. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Palace respects the Ombudsman’s decision as it is only performing its duties. “Iginagalang po natin ang aksyon ng Ombudsman dahil ito naman po ay nasa kanilang mandato (We respect the action of the Ombudsman because this is within its mandate),” she said. While the Palace had yet to receive a formal statement from President Marcos on the development, Castro said the President had already made clear his position on accountability. “Ang sa Pangulo naman po ay kung sino po ang dapat managot ay dapat na panagutin (The President’s position is that whoever should be held accountable should be held accountable),” she said. “Kung sino man po 'yan — kamag-anak, kaibigan, kaalyado, o kalaban sa pulitika (Whoever that may be — a relative, a friend, an ally, or a political opponent),” she added. Castro said the evidence should determine the course of the case, while those charged would have the opportunity to defend themselves. “Kung ano po ang isinisigaw ng ebidensya, dapat lamang po itong mailahad (Whatever the evidence shows, it should be brought to light),” she said. “Depende na po 'yan sa mga makakasuhan kung sila man po ay may sapat na ebidensya para ipaglaban ang kanilang sarili, nasa kanila na po 'yan (It will then be up to those charged, if they have sufficient evidence to defend themselves, to do so),” she added. Asked whether Marcos had expressed personal feelings about the case involving his cousin, Castro said she had not asked the President about it, but recalled his remarks during his fifth State of the Nation Address in July that he was prepared to let the evidence guide the government’s actions. “‘Pag ebidensya ang nagsusumigaw, kailangan po itong malaman ng taumbayan (When the evidence speaks, the people need to know about it),” she said. The Ombudsman filed the plunder case before the Sandiganbayan on Monday, accusing Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co of allegedly committing “concerted and coordinated acts” to unlawfully amass about P56 billion in ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Romualdez has repeatedly denied involvement in the alleged flood control anomalies and has said he is ready to face the charges and prove his side, while his legal team has questioned the evidence against him. The filing follows Marcos’ July SONA disclosure that the Ombudsman was preparing criminal cases against his cousin. “Masakit man sa akin ito, pero kailangan nating gawin ang tama (Painful as this may be for me, but we have to do what is right),” the President said. “Hindi ako pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako pangulo ng aking kaibigan. Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas at ang tungkulin ko ay sa inyo, ang aking mga kapwa Pilipino (I am not the president of my family. articles.title: Former UK PM Cameron keynotes 27th World Knowledge Forum
articles.summary: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The…

blocks.text: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order."

Against the backdrop of profound discussions on the thoughtful coexistence of humanity and Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cameron, the 75th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, will deliver his keynote address on "A New Order of Co-intelligence in the Age of AI."
Cameron is expected to draw from his experience in reviving the British economy through deregulatory and structural reforms following the 2008 global financial crisis.
He will offer strategic insights on the leadership required to navigate today's compounding crises defined by the AI revolution and heightened geopolitical uncertainty.

Also joining the roster of speakers in this year’s iteration of the WKF are Go Negosyo founder and Association of Southeast Asian Nations-Business Advisory Council (ASEAN-BAC) Chairman Jose Ma. Concepcion III who will also receive the ASEAN Entrepreneurs Award together with Don Lam, CEO of VinaCapital.

Other speakers are Cho Jung-sik, Speaker of the National Assembly, former Prime Minister of Denmark Helle Thorning-Schmidt, former Japanese Prime Minister Ishiba Shigeru, and former New York City Mayor Eric Adams.
This year's forum will bring together close to 70,000 participants and 6,303 world-renowned speakers from 86 countries to share fresh insights for humanity as we enter the era of AI.

Dr. Chang Dae-whan, WKF founder and chairman of the Maekyung Media, said the 27th World Knowledge Forum is being held at a critical juncture, as the established order driving global economic growth collapses and protectionism and geopolitical tensions intensify.
“Confronting low growth and unexpected leadership changes, South Korea urgently requires comprehensive innovation and bold challenges across all sectors.”
“In particular, rapid technological advancements led by AI are reshaping industry and politics, throwing humanity into a sweeping transformation,” Chang said.

He added that while major powers invest astronomical sums in technologies like semiconductors, quantum computing, and robotics, concerns are mounting over winner-takes-all monopolies and job displacement, further intensifying social conflicts.
To break through these simultaneous crises, Chang said Maeil Business Newspaper chose this year's main theme: “The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order.”

“The mythical ‘Promethean Moment’ signifies a historical turning point when humanity received ' fire '—a revolutionary tool that drove civilization forward, yet acted as a double-edged sword if left uncontrolled,” he said.
“Likewise, we hope humanity can overcome this civilizational upheaval brought by AI with wisdom, ultimately architecting a new order where technology and humanity coexist,” Chang added.

Prominent speakers at previous WKFs have included state leaders such as George W. Bush, the 43rd President of the United States; Theresa May, the 76th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom; Nicolas Sarkozy, the 23rd President of the French Republic; and Gerhard Schrfder, the 7th Chancellor of Germany. Presidents of international organizations have also participated, including Jim Yong Kim, the 12th President of the World Bank. Founders and CEOs such as Bill Gates, Co-founder of Microsoft Corporation; Larry Ellison, Chairman and CEO of Oracle Corporation; John L. Hennessy, Chairman of Alphabet; and George Soros, Chairman of Soros Fund Management, have graced the forum. Scholars including Larry Summers, Paul Krugman, Michael Porter, and Gregory Mankiw have also addressed the forum.

articles.title: Jhonny Bobier breaks silence on ‘Tatsulok’ controversy, says he was ‘intentionally humiliated’
articles.summary: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he…

blocks.text: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he screened it publicly using fake MTRCB permit. In a video statement sent to GMA News Online, Bobier denied having anything to do with the alleged falsified Permit to Exhibit (PTE) linked to “Tatsulok Trilogy” and Tanajuan Pelikula Production. “I had nothing to do with that alleged fake MTRCB permit. I do not know where it came from,” Bobier said, as quoted by GMA News Online. The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) earlier said “Tatsulok” had not undergone its review and classification process and had no valid PTE. The agency also said it discovered a fake permit connected to the film and its production company. Bobier, however, maintained that he never obtained an MTRCB permit for the film’s August 21 premiere. According to his account, this was his first time independently handling the requirements for a public film screening, after previously having such matters handled through film festivals. He said he relied on a Gateway Cineplex representative who handled the agreement for the screening and believed the cinema would inform him about the necessary requirements. Bobier also claimed he understood that a permit was needed for the planned August 29 public screening, not the August 21 premiere. The situation came to a head during the premiere when a cinema representative allegedly asked him for an MTRCB permit and warned that the screening could be stopped without one. Bobier said he decided to proceed with the event because the venue had already been paid for and guests were already waiting to watch the film. It was the timing of the issue that particularly troubled him. The director described the cinema management's decision to raise the permit concern at the last minute as suspicious, arguing that he should have been informed earlier if the document was a requirement. More importantly, Bobier said the incident left him feeling deliberately embarrassed in front of the people who had supported his film. “I cannot help but feel that they tried to humiliate me and embarrass me in front of those people who supported my film,” Bobier said. He further described the experience as being “intentionally cornered and humiliated,” saying it made him appear irresponsible for an administrative issue he claimed he did not create or know about. The filmmaker's comments come after Gateway Cineplex 18 issued a public notice on August 26 saying it was not associated with Tanajuan Pelikula or the planned August 29 screening of “Tatsulok.” The cinema also said the film would not be shown at any of its cinemas. Bobier said the notice prompted him to finally give his own account of what happened. He is now working with his lawyer and is seeking due process as the controversy continues.

articles.title: Government calamity spending surges 35% at end-August as disasters strike
articles.summary: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction…

blocks.text: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction requirements nationwide.

Data from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) showed that cumulative end-August releases jumped by 35.3 percent from the end-July total of ₱10.4 billion. As of Aug. 31, the available balance of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) stood at ₱26.1 billion.

This total is drawn from a ₱40.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2026—consisting of ₱23.5 billion for the NDRRM Program (NDRRMP), ₱15.3 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program (DRRAP) for local government units, and ₱1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund (PSF)—supplemented by ₱322.9 million in continuing appropriations from 2025.

To date, all disbursements have been sourced exclusively from the NDRRMP. The bulk, totaling ₱12.9 billion, was directed toward Quick Response Fund (QRF) augmentations for immediate relief and rehabilitation. Meanwhile, ₱1.1 billion was released for specific rehabilitation and logistics projects approved by the Office of the President (OP).
While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) was previously the sole recipient of QRF augmentations, several other national agencies have now received standby funds.

The DSWD remains the largest recipient, drawing ₱11.4 billion in total QRF replenishments across six tranches: ₱2 billion in February, ₱1.9 billion in March, ₱2 billion in April, ₱1.7 billion in June, ₱2 billion in July, and ₱1.8 billion in August.
Among other agencies receiving emergency funds, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) received ₱1.2 billion in August for its first QRF replenishment of the year.

The Department of National Defense (DND) received ₱300 million in July for the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) QRF, while the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) received ₱50 million in July for the Philippine National Police (PNP) QRF.

Apart from emergency relief, the ₱1.1 billion approved by the OP for targeted resilience projects includes ₱650 million for the DPWH to retrofit and strengthen the San Juanico Bridge in Region VIII, ₱385.1 million for the DND-OCD’s NDRRMC Integrated Logistics Hub at Lumbia Airport, and ₱44.8 million for DSWD command center repairs in Clark and rescue vehicle procurement.

Following these releases, the NDRRMP holds an available balance of ₱9.5 billion. When combined with the untouched DRRAP at ₱15.3 billion and the total PSF at ₱1.3 billion, the government retains ₱26.1 billion to address disaster-related and climate-mitigation requirements for the remaining four months of the year.

articles.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands…

blocks.text: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometers (90 miles) from Indonesia’s capital, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting hundreds of flights and leaving more than 170,000 passengers stranded, according to the transport ministry.

At least four airports, including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, extended their closure from Monday morning to 6:00 pm (1100 GMT), airport operator Angkasa Pura said in a social media post.

“In connection with the increasing eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, flight operations at several airports have been suspended; passengers are advised to regularly monitor their flight status with the respective airlines,” the operator said.
Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, also extended its closure, the company said.
The probability of an eruption remains high until Monday morning, the country’s geology agency said.

“The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues,” the agency said.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and left thousands displaced. /dl

articles.title: Butuan City declared under state of calamity due to water crisis
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425 families, or more than of its 269,000 residents, have been experiencing almost no-water service as water availability have continued to decline, particularly in the city's 11 most-populated barangays. Accordingly, the water shortage was linked to the prevailing dry spell in this capital city of Caraga region, which has experience a significant rainfall deficit. Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” H. Fortun ordered the implementation of water rationing in most affected areas, but these interventions have remainedinsufficient as the shortage continued. Fortun now centered the use of 30-percentQuick Response Fund to the most affected barangays. The state of calamity declaration is expected to allow the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access Quick Response Funds for emergency measures, including the provision and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps and filtration systems, as well as other equipment needed for water distribution and rationing. The state of calamity was declared over the weekend, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Third Special Session, the approval of SP Resolution No. 17-444-2026 at the City Hal Conference Room here. “The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP Resolution said. “We are doing our very best to address this problem,” Mayor Fortun said. The water crisis comes as Agusan del Norte and Butuan City, continues to experience a significant rainfall deficit. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) placed the province under “Dry Spell” status as of August 23, 2026.

articles.summary: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning…

blocks.text: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning incident.
Among those circulating online are songs dedicated to Rene, with some using AI-generated music and others appearing to be AI covers or altered versions of existing songs.
One example is “Kalapastanganan,” credited to fitterkarma, which has been re-presented as AI covers of various genres and styles.
Other Rene-related releases include “Baon ang Pangarap,” credited to Andrei AI Music and “Tribute for Rene Baterbonia” by Nihvan.
There are also other music uploads carrying Rene’s name or referencing his death, showing how his story has continued to circulate beyond social media and into streaming services.
There are also AI-generated videos featuring Baterbonia in different scenarios, from still playing basketball to rising out of waters to begging for social media interactions.

These digitally created clips have added another form of online remembrance surrounding the late athlete, with his likeness being used to depict moments and activities that did not necessarily occur in real life.

The growing collection of AI-generated and AI-assisted content has effectively created a digital archive of sorts around Rene, combining original tribute material, covers, edited imagery and fabricated video scenes.
Meanwhile, Rene’s mother continues to ask supporters to keep the focus on prayer and the family’s ongoing pursuit of justice.
In a Facebook post on September 5, Rovelyn asked supporters not to hold a large celebration or bring material offerings to her son’s grave for his 90th or 100th day commemoration.
“Gusto ko lang ng simpleng pagdasal,” she wrote, explaining that she wants to prioritize the case involving her son.
Rovelyn also said that people who wish to help the family financially may send voluntary assistance directly to her instead of bringing food, decorations or other material gifts.

She included her e-wallet details in the post and asked donors to provide screenshots of their transactions for verification. The request follows previous statements from Rovelyn concerning financial assistance and the use of her son's name.
Rovelyn has consistently maintained that justice remains her primary concern.
“Hustisya po ang hiling ko di po PERA,” she previously said, while expressing gratitude to those who continued to support the family.

articles.title: Breakneck finish looms as ICTSI Summit Point unfolds on Tuesday
articles.summary: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move. With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first…

blocks.text: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move.

With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first four legs producing three one-stroke finishes, another breakneck battle looms as the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets going Tuesday, Sept. 8, at the Summit Point Golf and Country Club here.

Quiban returns to the local circuit after a stint overseas, where he continued to sharpen his game following his stirring come-from-behind victory at Lakewood in the season’s opening leg. Que, meanwhile, is out to build on his clutch performance at Caliraya Springs, where he scrambled his way to a dramatic last-hole escape over fellow veteran Tony Lascuña.

And with Lloyd Go, winner of the last two legs at Pinewoods and Pradera Verde, opting to compete abroad in pursuit of added experience and game enhancement, the title chase has been thrown even wider open.
The stage is therefore set for another highly charged four-day shootout, with established stars, emerging talents and a growing band of contenders all capable of seizing the slightest opening.
Summit Point should provide the perfect test.

The course has held its own despite the recent mix of sun and rain, and while its well-maintained layout may look inviting, it can quickly turn daunting when approached without discipline. Softer fairways could encourage the Tour’s big hitters to attack more aggressively, but knowing when to unleash the power – and when to throttle back – could prove just as important.
The course rewards boldness, but it also exacts a price for even the slightest lapse in judgment.

Keanu Jahns leads the power-hitting charge, arriving with renewed confidence after a respectable finish in a rare Asian Development Tour event last month. The Fil-German, a four-time PGT leg winner who capped last season with the Match Play Championship, has been knocking on the door again and feels it is time to reclaim the spotlight.

Jahns opened the season with a third-place finish at Lakewood, followed it with sixth at Caliraya Springs, stumbled to joint 28th at Pinewoods, then bounced back with another third-place showing at Pradera Verde. He now hopes to turn that roller-coaster run into another victory at Summit Point.

Sean Ramos likewise enters the week with title aspirations. The young standout, who broke through for his first PGT victory in 2024, has spent the last two months competing overseas, further honing a game that increasingly looks ready for another championship run in the P2.5 million event organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc.
He is only one of a talented crop of young players determined to break through.

Carl Corpus has another PGT title firmly in his sights after claiming the Valley Golf leg last year. With the Asian Games looming later this month, Corpus is also using the event as an important competitive tune-up, seeking to find his rhythm early and build the form and confidence needed for the daunting Asiad challenge.

Aidric Chan brings a similar sense of purpose. The former national amateur standout has already secured his first professional victory on the ADT and is now chasing his maiden PGT triumph. Jeffren Lumbo and Russell Bautista are likewise expected to figure prominently in the mix.
But while the young guns bring hunger and momentum, Summit Point’s demanding conditions could tilt the balance toward experience.

That makes the presence of multi-titled campaigners Guido van der Valk, Rupert Zaragosa, Reymon Zaragosa, Jhonnel Ababa, Zanieboy Gialon, Michael Bibat, Jay Bayron and Lascuña all the more significant. Each knows how quickly a tournament can turn and, more importantly, when to press and when to protect a score.
The foreign contingent is equally determined to make its mark.

Korean Taewon Ha, who narrowly missed out at Lakewood, headlines the overseas challenge and returns with another opportunity to break through. Fellow Koreans Kim Tae Soo and Jisung Cheon, as well as Lee Song, are also in the hunt, alongside Japan’s Kashihara Hirotaka, Sena Shiraishi and Nagata Masaki.
With Go absent and no shortage of players carrying either momentum, unfinished business or a larger goal into the week, the Summit Point championship promises another wide-open affair.
The numbers already point to a tight battle. The course could make it even tighter.
And if the first four legs are any indication, expect the championship to be decided by the finest of margins.

Reyes Jr, Naval Command Western Mindanao Commander, commended the operating units and partner agencies for their coordination and vigilance which led to the successful conduct of operations. “These operations reflect NCWM’s sustained commitment to securing the maritime domain of Western Mindanao and preventing its use for smuggling and other illegal activities,” Reyes said.

articles.title: Europe wrestles with impact of historic regional gains for Germany's AfD
articles.summary: The BBC's Europe editor Katya Adler sees the far-right win in Saxony-Anhalt state ringing alarm bells for the EU and traditional parties.

blocks.text: "Seismic", "a socio-political earthquake", "a watershed moment for Germany".

This was how political analysts and many media outlets described the stunning victory of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in local elections in Germany on Sunday. Is that an exaggeration?

Saxony-Anhalt is one of the smallest of massive Germany's 16 regions. It boasts a mere 1.7m out of 59m eligible voters nationwide. How significant can its political sentiments be, especially since the AfD narrowly failed to win an outright majority?
The answer: very significant.
First and foremost, at home in Germany.

The vote may have been regional but it impacts at national level. The AfD landslide piles even more pressure on the already beleaguered centrist coalition government in Berlin. It may prove to be the nail in the political coffin of Germany's deeply unpopular conservative Chancellor, Friedrich Merz. He had promised to slash the AfD's popularity.

These political woes will further weaken and distract Germany, the EU's most powerful player, at a time of continental crisis - as Europe struggles to contain Russian aggression, Donald Trump's tariff tantrums and the economic threat from China.

The Saxony-Anhalt result also provokes soul-searching throughout Germany, where the Nazi past still looms large. This is the first outstanding electoral landslide for a hard right nationalist party since the fall of the Third Reich in 1945.
The German authorities have labelled the AfD, in part, anti-democratic and a number of regional factions of the party, including Saxony-Anhalt, far right extremist.
The AfD is well known to be particularly popular in east Germany but it's now also polling as the biggest political party nationwide.
Germany's political mainstream has failed voters, it would seem. What does Europe's biggest single economy, its most populous nation not counting Russia, do now?
Tiny Saxony-Anhalt is causing waves outside Germany too.
None other than the President of the United States swiftly posted the Saxony-Anhalt exit poll on his Truth Social platform on Sunday.

The AfD's anti-immigration, anti-woke, "Germany for Germans" message chimes closely with Donald Trump's MAGA missive. Along with a number of other nationalist parties in Europe, the AfD borrows heavily from the Trump playbook - undermining mainstream media, questioning the neutrality of judges and promising to "make Germany great again".
Interesting to note though - the US president is rarely name-checked on the campaign trail in Europe. Politicians are keenly aware just how unpopular he is amongst voters.

Hot on Donald Trump's social media heels on Sunday night was the influential Russian businessman Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of the Russian Direct Investment Fund. He declared the AfD result "historic", Germany's national government "discredited" and the German Chancellor "humiliated", comparing Friedrich Merz to the UK's not-long-gone prime minister, Keir Starmer, who felt forced to resign this summer.
What interest might Russia have in German regional elections, you might ask, and what was Dmitriev's dig at the UK all about?
The German government is the largest single donor to Ukraine and the UK is known to have provided Kyiv with missiles used to strike inside Russian territory. This has deeply angered Moscow.

The AfD, by comparison, is pretty pro-Russia. It wants to stop sending military aid to Ukraine, halt sanctions against Moscow and start buying much cheaper Russian energy again. Energy-hungry German industry suffered a huge economic blow after the country halted Russian energy imports, following the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The AfD's softly-softly approach to Russia has another appeal in Germany's east, which remains far poorer than the west. This, despite Germany spending between 2.3 and 3 trillion euros (depending on reports and whether inflation is taken into account) to help integrate the former communist part of the country after the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall.

Saxony-Anhalt is Germany's poorest region and there, as in much of east Germany, you often encounter what's known as "Ostalgie" amongst voters; essentially "nostalgia in the east" for comparatively more stable times under communism.

Also watching the Saxony-Anhalt election closely was the European Union. The next 12 months is bumper election season across the EU. Ballots are expected in key nations France, Italy, Spain and Poland. Brussels fears more "extreme" parties, left but particularly right of the political spectrum, may benefit across the board.
The leader of Spain's nationalist Vox party, Santiago Abascal, posted on X on Sunday that the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt was " a great hope for Germany and for Europe".

By contrast, France's Europe Minister, Benjamin Haddad, an ally of centrist President Emmanuel Macron, warned "this is a serious moment in Europe, seeing the far right win in a regional election in Germany".

Neither the AfD, nor other European parties labelled "extreme right" or "hard right", accept the label. They also differ from one another in tone and party programme. France's National Rally under Marine Le Pen kicked the AfD out of its grouping in the European Parliament two years ago, for being too "radical". What the parties do tend to share, however, is an anti-immigration platform and strong nationalist messaging. And that really worries the EU.

Whether it's a rallying cry for "Germany First" or "Italy First" or "France for the French!", the concern in Brussels is that the rise of nationalist parties strains European cohesion at a time when outside events demand it more than ever.

Nationalist parties like the AfD or Italy's League Party tend to be deeply Eurosceptic, but Brussels says Europe needs to stand united to counter Donald Trump's bullying, for example, or to effectively protect European business against China's goods dumping.

Europe's defence establishment also warns that fractures in European sanctions against Russia or countries going tepid on Nato membership (as you see in Marine Le Pen's National Rally for example, or Germany's AfD) just emboldens Moscow.
Security chiefs say nations must stick together to stop Russia in Ukraine, otherwise the Kremlin will be tempted to attack inside Nato, such as the Baltic states.

The thing is, Europe's voters are very aware of these outside threats and the impact they have at home. They worry about the impact of wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, about crumbling health services at home and dwindling economic security for themselves and their family. Uncontrolled immigration and safety on the streets are huge concerns too.

And this is where the significance of the Saxony-Anhalt vote shines bright. A flashing red warning to traditional political parties, but also to institutions across Europe like the judiciary and security services. Those the AfD dismisses as the self-interested "Establishment".

Voters on this continent feel lost and let down by parties they've supported over and again for decades. Looking right or left now at election time does not mean they've all suddenly become extremist.

The AfD campaign slogan in Saxony-Anhalt was an upbeat "Anything is Possible!" Plus a promise to make Germans feel proud of their country again. Till now untried and untested in government, people seem increasingly willing to give them a go.

articles.title: After US Open, Eala sets sights on Singapore tourney
articles.summary: Alex Eala will have plenty of time to rest for her next competition following her third-round finish at the US Open in New York over the weekend. The 21-year-old Eala is listed to compete in the…

blocks.text: Alex Eala will have plenty of time to rest for her next competition following her third-round finish at the US Open in New York over the weekend. The 21-year-old Eala is listed to compete in the Singapore Open, a WTA 500 event scheduled on Sept. 21 to 27 at the OCBC Arena. It served as the first tournament in the Asian swing. Based on the latest player list, the tournament draws three of the world’s top 10 players in No. 3 Jessica Pegula, No. 5 and French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, as well as No. 10 and two-time Grand Slam finalist Amanda Anisimova. Other players also competing are two-time Grand Slam champion Barbora Krejcikova, Anastasia Potapova, Donna Vejic and fellow Southeast Asian standout Janice Tjen of Indonesia. The tournament also serves as a prelude to Eala’s reported participation in the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where competition starts on Sept. 27 to Oct. 2. Currently ranked No. 18, Eala hopes to ride on the momentum of her strong run over the past months, that include her historic fourth-round finish at the Wimbledon, winning her breakthrough WTA title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, DC, and her third-round finish at the US Open.
