articles.title: PVL: Nxled fends off Ho Chi Minh City to stay in race to final
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.…

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons’ Jonah Sabete-Escamillan rises for a hit during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines — Nxled turned back Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City, 25-20, 31-33, 25-17, 25-22, to stay in finals contention in the PVL Invitational Conference on Friday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.

Jonah Sabete-Escamillan continued to display an all-around game with 18 points, 20 excellent receptions, and 15 digs. Myla Pablo also scored 18, highlighted by five blocks, while MJ Phillips chipped in 17 points.
Gel Cayuna dished out 35 excellent sets, as EJ Laure-Cariño had 16 points and 24 excellent receptions, while Jackie Acuña added 12, as Nxled tied PLDT at 2-2.
Nxled, which battles Farm Fresh on Sunday at 1:30 p.m., holds the tie-break advantage with seven points ahead of PLDT’s six.

Hours after a five-set meltdown to EST Cola on Thursday night when they blew a 20-12 lead in the fourth set, the Chameleons squandered another big lead against the Vietnamese, who erased their 19-10 margin and cut it down to one, 22-21, after Dang Thi Kim Thanh’s kill.

blocks.caption: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference.

blocks.text: Nxled Chameleons during a game vs Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City in the PVL Invitational Conference. –MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
Phillips and Escamillan refused to suffer the same heartbreak, closing out the game with three points including two quick attacks from the former.

“We love to fight because the last game was a five set and it was only a few hours ago. It was really tough and we wanted immediately to show that we never back down, we are not broken, we will never be broken after a losing match and we are ready to fight,” said Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti.

“Obviously, there are bad things and good things. The good thing is this one: we never give up. The bad thing is that we are developing the side out, but we can do even better because sometimes, I joke about this, our side out is kind of bipolar or we play like a super great team or we get scared and under pressure and nothing works, and so it’s a part of the mental game that we have to really develop.”
Dang led the Vietnamese with 15 points and 15 digs. The 16-year-old Ho Thi Bich Diep had 13 points, while Dao Thi Nhung added 11.
Ho Chi Minh bombed out of finals contention with a 1-3 record.

articles.title: Dalaguete vegetable farmer on motorbike shot, killed
articles.summary: A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu....…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 29-year-old farmer was shot dead in a violent ambush while driving his motorcycle loaded with baskets of fresh vegetables on Thursday evening, September 3, in Barangay Nalhub, Dalaguete, Cebu.

Police identified the victim as alias “JR,” a farmer and resident of Barangay Nalhub. Investigators confirmed that the victim died instantly at the scene after sustaining multiple gunshot wounds to various parts of his body.
The incident occurred around 7:15 p.m. while the victim was transporting his produce along the road.
The Dalaguete Municipal Police Station immediately launched an investigation after receiving a call from the Barangay Chairman of Nalhub reporting the shooting.
Initial police findings revealed that the victim was actively maneuvering his motorcycle—which was carrying vegetable baskets (locally known as bukag)—when he was fired upon.
Probe in progress
At the crime scene, forensic investigators recovered two empty shell casings believed to be from a .45 caliber handgun, as well as two misfired rounds of ammunition.
The perpetrator remains unidentified and fled the scene following the attack.
The Dalaguete Police are continuing their investigation to determine the motive and trace the whereabouts of the suspect.

articles.title: Cebuana Lhuillier turns purposeful communication into impact at the Philippine Quill Awards
articles.summary: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education,…

blocks.text: Cebuana Lhuillier is demonstrating how strategic communication can go beyond telling a company’s story to creating value for the people it reaches. Through its workplace, financial education, entrepreneurship, and advocacy platforms, the company uses communication to address real needs, create opportunities, and encourage people to learn, participate, and take action.

This approach earned the company Merit recognition at the 22nd Philippine Quill Awards across four areas: Internal Communication for Amazing KaCebuana; Corporate Social Responsibility for Money Guro and Happiest Pinoy; Government Relations and Public Affairs for its range of Business Support solutions; and Social Media for Money Guro.

For Cebuana Lhuillier President and CEO Jean Henri Lhuillier, effective communication should create value for the people it reaches. “At Cebuana Lhuillier, communication is not just about telling people what we do. It is about creating something useful for the people we serve,” said Lhuillier. “When communication helps an employee feel valued, gives a Filipino knowledge to make better decisions, equips an entrepreneur to grow, or gives people a reason to believe in themselves and each other, then it has done its job.”
Purpose Across Every Platform
That principle is reflected in each of the company’s recognized initiatives, with every platform built around a distinct audience need.

Within the organization, Amazing KaCebu integrates employee engagement into the everyday work experience. Through platforms such as Workvivo and the Corporate News Ngayon newsletter, which connects thousands of employees across the country, along with the Brillo Awards, leadership programs, and the REBEL wellbeing app, employees have more ways to stay informed, be recognized, be heard, and feel supported.

For navigating everyday financial decisions, Money Guro makes financial education more accessible and relatable by turning complex concepts into practical conversations. Through social media, student engagements, workshops, and even Roblox, it brings financial education closer to Filipinos.

Happiest Pinoy takes a different approach, using storytelling to reflect the Filipino experience. Its 2025 campaign moved beyond the search for a single “happiest” Filipino and opened the platform to stories of hope, recovery, and resilience, giving people space to share experiences and find connection through a shared sense of community.

For entrepreneurs, Cebuana Lhuillier’s suite of business support solutions recognizes that capital is only one part of what MSMEs need to grow. Its digital-first ecosystem brings together business education, expert guidance, tools, mentoring, entrepreneur stories, and financial services to help business owners make better decisions and build capability at every stage of their journey.
What connects these initiatives is a simple approach: start with what people need, then find the right way to reach them.

“What makes these initiatives stand out is how each one starts with a clear audience need and translates it into a communication approach that people can relate to and act on,” said Emirosco Michael Sena, First Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer of Cebuana Lhuillier. “Whether we are engaging our employees, simplifying financial concepts, supporting entrepreneurs, or telling stories of resilience, we look at the right message, platform, and format for each audience. The Merit Awards validate that approach and the work of our teams in turning strong ideas into programs that deliver results.”
Communication That Moves People

Organized by the International Association of Business Communicators (IABC) Philippines, the Philippine Quill Awards recognize excellence in business communication, including strategic thinking, creative execution, and results.

For Cebuana Lhuillier, the recognition reinforces the role communication can play beyond corporate messaging. Done with purpose, it can help employees feel connected, make knowledge more accessible, strengthen entrepreneurs, and create space for stories that matter.
Ultimately, the goal is not simply to be heard. It is to create communication that leaves people with something they can use, act on, or carry forward.
ADVT.
This article is brought to you by Cebuana Lhuillier.

articles.title: Zheng Qinwen back in the hunt–and US Open third round
articles.summary: NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of…

blocks.text: FILE–Qinwen Zheng of China. (AP Photo/Maja Smiejkowska)

NEW YORK– Zheng Qinwen flopped to the court then jumped up in a fist-pumping celebration Thursday after battling into the US Open third round, the 2024 Olympic gold medalist relishing the return of her game — and her competitive fire.
The former world number four endured an injury-plagued 2025 that included a longer than anticipated recovery from elbow surgery.
She missed the Australian Open and has struggled to regain her form, and the mindset of a champion.
“Before the surgery, for me winning is like drinking water — everything comes natural, everything comes fluent,” Zheng said after beating Yulia Putintseva 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 to reach the third round.
“After my surgery, I had some tough matches against the best players in the world (and) I’m close but I don’t get them.
“I totally lost the dynamic of how to compete.
“Now after two, three months I really felt the first time in this tournament I find myself, I found my fire back during the competition.”
Zheng sank so far in the rankings that she had to go through qualifying to book her US Open berth.
She grudgingly acknowledged that grinding through the qualifiers may have helped her regain her competitive edge — but that didn’t really take the sting away.
“It takes a while for me to accept my ranking dropped to 125 and, OK, I need to actually play qualies,” she said.
Now she’s in the thick of the main draw and will face former Australian Open champion Keys for a place in the last 16.
Zheng is looking forward to the test — and likely a chance to step back onto one of the main show courts of Flushing Meadows after toiling through two rounds on the outside courts.
“I used to always play on the big court,” she said. “I need to fight to get everything back.”

articles.title: Yvon Bisera shooting for two birds at LPGT Summit Point stop
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City…

blocks.text: Yvon Bisera has two wins in the LPGT season thus far. CONTRIBUTED PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines–In-form Yvon Bisera seeks a third Ladies PGT title this season, teeing off as the solid favorite when the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets off the ground Tuesday in Lipa City in Batangas.
Bisera will not just be seeking to win another P1 million event, but also use this stint to sharpen her game for a first appearance in the lucrative yet tougher Korean LPGA later this month.

“I want to play well at Summit Point and use it to prepare for Korea,” said Bisera, who will play in the Hana Financial Group Championship from Sept. 17-20 in Gyeonggi Province, on Daebudo Island southwest of Seoul.

Bisera has been in impressive form on the LPGT this season, outlasting two rivals in a playoff to capture the Lakewood Championship in March. She then produced an emphatic seven-shot victory at the Pradera Verde Championship last July, and those victories have certainly established her as a favorite in Lipa.
With her Korean LPGA debut fast approaching, Bisera has used her time between tournaments to fine-tune the part of her game she believes could prove decisive at Summit Point: the short game.

While waiting for her Korean visa documents, the Davaoeña has devoted extra time to sharpening her touch around the greens, particularly with the possibility of strong winds adding another layer of difficulty at the Batangas layout.
“You can’t lose focus at Summit Point, especially in the face of strong winds,” Bisera continued in Filipino.
That focus will be particularly crucial in a 54-hole event, where a fast start can provide early advantage.
Bisera, however, is not expecting another runaway performance like the one she produced at Pradera Verde.
“I really want to win, but everyone in the field has been preparing hard for this tournament,” she said. “But I will try my best to perform well for my confidence going to Korea.”

She will have plenty of opposition in Batangas, with reigning Order of Merit champion Sarah Ababa leading a compact but formidable field that also features former leg winners Mafy Singson, Tiffany Lee, Chihiro Ikeda and Princess Superal.

Korean challenger Kim Seoyun is likewise expected to figure prominently, along with title-hungry contenders Martina Miñoza, Pamela Mariano, Velinda Castil, Rev Alcantara, Angela Mangana and Gretchen Villacencio.

articles.title: Cebu, Bohol anti-drug ops target 129 cannabis, ₱238K shabu
articles.summary: Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Authorities uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants in Toledo City, Cebu, and arrested a drug personality in a buy-bust operation that yielded around 35 grams of shabu in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, in separate anti-illegal drug operations on Thursday, September 3.
The operations were conducted by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 7 (PDEA 7), Philippine National Police (PNP) units and other law enforcement agencies.
Marijuana in Toledo
Around 11:08 a.m., combined law enforcement elements uprooted 129 fully grown marijuana plants from a cultivation site in Sitio Guincamote, Barangay Captain Claudio, Toledo City.
Authorities reached the site after an over eight-hour trek.
The operation stemmed from information provided by a confidential informant, followed by about one month of case buildup, according to authorities.

The operation involved personnel from the PDEA Cebu Provincial Office, Naval Forces Central, PNP Drug Enforcement Group–Special Operations Unit 7, Cebu Provincial Police Office–Provincial Intelligence Unit, CPPO–2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company, and Toledo City Police Station.
PDEA 7 identified the suspected cultivator as alias Gene, a resident of Barangay Captain Claudio, who fled the scene before authorities could arrest him.
The 129 marijuana plants had an estimated value of ₱25,800.

Representative samples of the seized plants were turned over to the PDEA 7 Regional Office Laboratory, while the remaining plants were burned on site following protocols established for the disposition of dangerous drugs.
Authorities said a case for cultivation of dangerous drugs under Section 16, Article II of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, will be filed against Gene.
Shabu in Tagbilaran
Later that day, around 5:24 p.m., authorities arrested another drug personality in a buy-bust operation at Purok 4, Barangay Bool, Tagbilaran City, Bohol.
The operation was conducted by the PDEA Bohol Provincial Office, Tagbilaran Police Station and Bohol Maritime Police.

Authorities acted on information from a confidential informant and conducted about one week of case buildup before the buy-bust operation.The suspect was identified as alias Kalaw, 38, unemployed and a resident of Barangay Tangnan, Panglao, Bohol.
Seized during the operation were three packs of shabu weighing around 35 grams, with an estimated average market value of ₱238,000.
Authorities also seized the buy-bust money and a cell phone.
Authorities said Kalaw had allegedly been disposing of around 50 grams of shabu weekly.
The seized dangerous drugs were turned over to the PNP Bohol Forensic Unit for proper disposition.
As of Friday, September 4, Kalaw remains in the custody of the Tagbilaran Police Station.
He is set to face charges for the sale and possession of dangerous drugs under Sections 5 and 11, Article II of Republic Act 9165.
The two operations resulted in the seizure of illegal drugs with a combined estimated value of ₱263,800, including the ₱25,800 worth of marijuana plants and ₱238,000 worth of shabu.

articles.title: Yeng Constantino says husband Victor doesn’t get jealous of Ryan Bang
articles.summary: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.…

blocks.text: Yeng Constantino clarified that her husband, Victor “Yan” Asuncion, does not get jealous of Ryan Bang, whose past with the singer recently resurfaced following an emotional moment at her concert.

Constantino was asked during an ambush interview after the media conference for “The Voice Kids” on Friday, Sept. 4, in Quezon City, whether her husband minds that her and Bang’s courting history recently renewed attention online.

“Sana nga nagseselos eh,” she joked. “Hindi nya kasi personality. Talagang ano sya, very understanding. Kilalang kilala kasi ako ng asawa ko. Alam nya ‘yung pagkanta ko kay Ryan ay nangungulit lamang ako. Actually, mas nakaka-emphatize nga siya kay Ryan kaysa sa akin.”
Constantino said Asuncion and Bang are not close friends, but she hopes that one day, the three of them will get to hang out together.
The story stemmed from Constantino “Biyaheng Bente: 20th Anniversary Concert” on Aug. 28, where she serenaded Bang and recalled their “almost” romance from their early years in show business.
Constantino previously revealed that she had a huge crush on Ryan but felt hurt when he stopped pursuing her.
Bang, for his part, explained that he thought the singer was not interested in him as he admitted that he was also “financially incapable” of dating someone at the time.
After the concert, Bang became emotional during the Sept. 2 episode of “It’s Showtime” while recalling his experience at Constantino’s concert.
He thanked Vice Ganda for bringing him to the show, saying it brought back good memories.
Bang, who has since become single following his split from former fiancée Paola Huyong earlier this year, wondered whether he would ever find someone like Constantino again.
Constantino said she did not expect her playful interaction with Bang at the concert to have such an emotional impact, noting that now she feels slightly regretful about singing to him.

“I was being playful. Hindi ko nga rin po alam ang naging resulta ng aking aksyon. At nag-cost nga na maungkat ang mga sugat. I’m really regretful din in a way. Siyempre nakita mo yung tao na may mga naalala siya. Nakasakit sa kanya. Masakit. Kasi ako, parang nagbibiro ako. Hindi ako nakapag-isip ng maayos to consider his feelings,” she said.
The “Chinito” singer noted that she had already reached out to Bang to apologize.

“Nag-message na po kami sa kanya. Talagang grabe ang sorry ko sa kanya. Ang haba po ng mga nobelang messages namin ni Ryan. Patawarin nyo po ako. Sorry talaga. Hindi ko alam na ganito. And it was really vulnerable. I really apologized for triggering some memories or moments in life namin. I wasn’t very mindful also,” she said.
When asked about Bang’s remark that he hoped he would someday find someone like Constantino, the singer assured him that he would find love.
“Siyempre naman. Naku, makakahanap at makakahanap si Ryan. Hindi deserve ni Ryan na questionin niya ang kanyang worth,” she said.

“Sa pagkakakilala ko po kay Ryan, talagang napakabait po na tao. What a good man. God has perfect timing for everybody. He deserves to be loved, to be cared for, to be seen. He deserves all of that,” she expressed.
Meanwhile, Constantino is one of the new judges of “The Voice Kids,” alongside Gloc-9 and returning judge Julie Anne San Jose. The new season premieres on GMA on Sept. 13. /apl

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines— Gilas Pilipinas saw a familiar face in Korea during its preparation for the 2026 Asian Games. In a Facebook post by Adrian Nocum, the Nationals were seen dining with Anyang JKJ’s…

blocks.text: KBL standout Rhenz Abando and Gilas Pilipinas players bound for the Asian Games. –ADRIAN NOCUM
MANILA, Philippines— Gilas Pilipinas saw a familiar face in Korea during its preparation for the 2026 Asian Games.
In a Facebook post by Adrian Nocum, the Nationals were seen dining with Anyang JKJ’s Filipino import and former Gilas swingman Rhenz Abando.
“Kain po tayo,” wrote Nocum in a post that also featured Converge twin towers Justin Arana and Justine Baltazar, Barangay Ginebra’s RJ Abarrientos and San Miguel Beer’s Don Trollano.
Nocum’s post gained traction among netizens, with some even speculating that Abando could be a last-minute addition to Gilas to replace the questionable Justin Brownlee.
No such news, however, has been confirmed, as the meal was simply a reunion since Abando is staying in Korea for his stint in the KBL.
Abando last suited up for Gilas in the 2023 Fiba World Cup.
Coincidentally, Nocum and Abando’s meeting was an NCAA reunion of sorts, as they faced each other in the Season 97 Finals between Mapua and Letran.
Since then, Abando joined the KBL, while Nocum declared for the PBA Draft before ultimately being selected by Rain or Shine.

articles.title: MIMAROPA cops, DENR seize P63.7K worth of forest products in one day
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police and environment authorities arrested two people and seized forest products worth an estimated over P63,000 in separate anti-illegal logging operations in…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police and environment authorities arrested two people and seized forest products worth an estimated over P63,000 in separate anti-illegal logging operations in Romblon and Palawan on Thursday (Sept. 3).

The Police Regional Office in MIMAROPA said the operations were conducted with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to curb illegal cutting and possession of forest products in the region.
MIMAROPA covers the southwestern Tagalog region composed of Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon and Palawan.

In San Fernando town in Romblon, personnel of the San Fernando Municipal Police Station provided security assistance to the DENR-Protected Area Management Office in Sibuyan during an anti-illegal logging operation in Sitio Olango, Barangay España.
At about 9:45 a.m., a 40-year-old resident was reportedly caught holding an axe beside a freshly-cut Balaw tree measuring about 30 centimeters in diameter and 30 feet long.
The tree was estimated to have a volume of 273.9 board feet, with a value of P13,695.
The suspect was brought to the San Fernando police station.

Authorities prepared charges against the arrested person for alleged violation of Section 77 of Presidential Decree No. 705, or the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines, as amended by Executive Order No. 277.
Meanwhile, in Palawan town of Roxas, the personnel of the Roxas Municipal Police Station enforced a search warrant against a 69-year-old resident of Purok Zambales in Barangay 3.
They moved together with the DENR, Palawan Provincial Intelligence Unit, and 2nd Provincial Mobile Force Company.
The warrant was issued in connection with an alleged violation of Section 77 of PD 705.
Authorities recovered assorted forest products, including Ipil lumber and planted Mahogany trees, with an estimated combined volume of 300 board feet and market value of P50,000.
Police said the suspect failed to present valid documents, permits or licenses authorizing the possession and ownership of the forest products.
The seized items were inventoried in the presence of barangay and media workers.
The suspect was brought to the Roxas police station. /apl

articles.title: Globe helps parents guide children's digital journey with GPlan Junior
articles.summary: As children spend more time online for learning, communication, entertainment, and everyday activities, many parents are looking for ways to support their growing digital needs while maintaining…

blocks.text: As children spend more time online for learning, communication, entertainment, and everyday activities, many parents are looking for ways to support their growing digital needs while maintaining appropriate guidance and oversight.
GPlan Junior was created to give kids the freedom to stay connected while giving parents greater peace of mind.
— Jo Anne Illescas-Pique
Senior Director for Globe Postpaid

To help families navigate this stage, Globe has introduced GPlan Junior, a dedicated postpaid line designed for dependents aged 7 to 20 years old. Available as an additional line under an existing Globe Postpaid Plan 999 and above, the offering provides reliable connectivity for children and students while allowing parents and legal guardians to manage the account under their supervision.

The initiative reflects Globe’s commitment to strengthening family connectivity by helping parents support their children’s digital experiences during the years when independence is growing but adult guidance remains important.

blocks.caption: GPlan Junior helps families keep children connected while giving parents greater visibility and control over their digital experiences. | Photo by Globe

blocks.text: For Php499 per month, GPlan Junior comes with unlimited calls and texts, 100-minutes of landline calls, 10GB of all-access data, free access to Messenger Kids and Mobile Legends, and unlimited access to three selected apps across video, social, and gaming categories.
Families may choose one app from each category:

items: Video: YouTube Kids, Netflix, Disney+, or Viu
Social: Viber or WhatsApp
Play: PUBG, Call of Duty, Discord, or Roblox

blocks.text: By linking a dependent’s mobile line to a parent’s Globe Postpaid account, GPlan Junior addresses the need for frequent reloads and monitoring expiring prepaid promos. This allows families to enjoy a more seamless connectivity experience while helping ensure that children remain connected when they need to be.

The plan’s 10GB-swappable data and with roll-over feature open access data and unlimited access to selected apps support the online activities that many children and students engage in daily, from messaging and video streaming to gaming and communication. At the same time, families benefit from more predictable monthly connectivity spending and reduced concerns about unexpected usage.

Parents can also monitor their child’s data usage through the GlobeOne app, allowing them to track consumption, view remaining allocations, and select Unli Apps, and the preferred Data Swap option. This gives families greater visibility and control while helping children develop more mindful and responsible digital activities and behaviors.

“As children become more connected, parents are looking for solutions that keep up with their family’s evolving needs,” said Jo Anne Illescas-Pique, Senior Director for Globe Postpaid. “GPlan Junior was created to give kids the freedom to stay connected while giving parents greater peace of mind through a simple, reliable Postpaid experience. It’s another way Globe is making technology work better for families and helping them stay connected to what matters most.”
Beyond connectivity, Globe is also encouraging families to build responsible digital and financial habits through an exclusive GCash Jr. incentive.

Eligible GPlan Junior subscribers who successfully sign up for GCash Jr. may receive up to Php500 worth of GCash vouchers. The initiative supports parents who want to introduce children to responsible money management and digital financial literacy at an early age while guiding how they learn, spend, save, and engage with digital financial tools in a supervised environment.

Together, GPlan Junior and GCash Jr. support Globe’s broader goal of helping families navigate an increasingly connected world with greater confidence while fostering responsible digital citizenship among the next generation.

Parents or legal guardians interested in applying may visit any Globe Store and present any proof of eligibility, including a copy of the dependent’s PSA Birth Certificate and a valid ID, such as a school ID or passport, to verify guardianship and age.
For more information, visit the nearest Globe Store or go to globe.com.ph.

articles.title: 2 deaths recorded in Olongapo due to leptospirosis
articles.summary: OLONGAPO CITY — As flooding persisted in several areas in this city, two people died of leptospirosis, based on data from the Olongapo City Health Office. As of Sept. 3, the city had recorded 27…

blocks.text: OLONGAPO CITY — As flooding persisted in several areas in this city, two people died of leptospirosis, based on data from the Olongapo City Health Office.
As of Sept. 3, the city had recorded 27 leptospirosis cases, of which 18 remained active.
Fourteen of the active cases were admitted at hospitals, four were being treated as outpatients, while seven patients have recovered from the disease.
The local government and the city health office reminded residents to avoid wading or playing in floodwaters, especially if they have open wounds.

The health office said free doxycycline was available at its office and at all barangay health centers for residents who had been submerged in floodwaters or those might need to wade through floods again.
Residents were advised to consult health personnel before taking doxycycline for proper use and dosage. /apl

articles.title: Teachers for barangay elections: DepEd Mandaue on prep mode
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) in Mandaue City is preparing teachers who may be tapped to serve in the November Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).... Keep on reading: Teachers…

blocks.text: MANDAUE CITY, Cebu — The Department of Education (DepEd) in Mandaue City is preparing teachers who may be tapped to serve in the November Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

Edgar Espina, administrative officer of the DepEd Mandaue City Schools Division, said the department has been coordinating with the Commission on Elections and is prepared to provide the teachers needed for the elections.

“DepEd is really prepared with the election. Andam na ta daan sa gipangayo sa Comelec, naghuwat ra pod ta if madayon o dili basta we have to continue our job, we will not stop kung unsa ang mandate sa DepEd, we will continue. Nag-agad ra pod tas taas if madayon o dili basta kami we are working for it mahuman amoang trabaho with regards to BSKE, Espina said.
(We are ready for whatever Comelec may ask of us; we are only waiting to know if the elections push through. We await the word of the higherups but we have to finish our job.)
Marshaling of frontliners
Espina said the teachers are currently being asked to signify their interest in serving in the elections, while the specific schedules for seminars and orientations will depend on the Comelec.
He said the number that will be sought by Comelec would likely be more than 1,000 teachers basing on previous elections.
Espina said that there were already initial schedules for teachers orientations but the division is awaiting if the elections push through.
Espina said teachers who have relatives involved in local politics may be assigned to another barangay to avoid possible conflicts of interest.
Responsive volunteers
He added that while election service is voluntary, teachers have historically responded to the need for personnel during elections and many continue to serve when called upon.
The preparations come as the November 2026 BSKE remains on the electoral calendar, although there have been proposals seeking to postpone the polls.

Senate Bill No. 2387, sponsored by Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero, seeks to set the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials at five years, which would move the scheduled November 2026 elections to November 2028.

The last BSKE was held in October 2023 and was originally expected to be held again in 2025. The elections were postponed to November 2026 after the terms of incumbent barangay and SK officials were extended to four years.

articles.title: Alex Eala’s growing star power draws US media attention
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–Filipino tennis star Alex Eala continues to be the talk of the town as her meteoric rise draws attention from some of the United States’ biggest publications. Eala landed on the…

blocks.text: Alex Eala Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, reacts during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships against Oleksandra Oliynykova, of Ukraine, Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in New York
MANILA, Philippines–Filipino tennis star Alex Eala continues to be the talk of the town as her meteoric rise draws attention from some of the United States’ biggest publications.

Eala landed on the front page of The New York Times for its September 3 print issue, highlighting her impact on the Filipino community at home and overseas, particularly in Queens, where the US Open is being held.

“But for Filipinos, she is not simply an ambassador for the sport. Her success is giving the country, a large, dispersed archipelago of more than 7,000 islands in Southeast Asia, as well as its diaspora, a reason to unite,” the article said.
Eala also landed an in-depth feature in Vogue, which highlighted the growing frenzy around the 21-year-old star and the Filipino fans who have followed her matches.

blocks.caption: Fans of Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, spell out "GO ALEX" with letters before her match against Mary Stoiana, of the United States, in the first round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, in New York.

blocks.text: Fans of Alexandra Eala, of the Philippines, spell out “GO ALEX” with letters before her match against Mary Stoiana, of the United States, in the first round of the U.S. Open tennis championships Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)
Forbes, meanwhile, noted Eala’s growing commercial value and projected that she could become one of the world’s highest-paid female athletes.

“I feel very confident that by 2027, she will be the second-highest-paid female athlete in the world, behind Coco [Gauff],” Max Eisenbud, head of client representation at WME Sports and its subsidiary IMG Tennis, was quoted as saying.
She also graced the digital cover of Sports Illustrated, which dubbed her “tennis’s next great superstar,” while The New Yorker published a story on how Eala “became a symbol of the Philippines.”
The stories have highlighted Eala’s rise to prominence and how it has helped Filipinos once again find someone to rally behind, much like during the heyday of Filipino boxing legend Manny Pacquiao.
Eala has been vocal about knowing what it means to carry the country wherever she goes, and fans have reciprocated that love by filling the stands during her tournaments.

“I think everybody represents something in their own way. I’m Filipino and I proudly represent that and a lot of the crowd here today is Filipino and I’m sure they share in that sentiment,” Eala said after her second-round victory at the US Open.
Eala continues her campaign in the last Grand Slam tournament of the season in the third round.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after disaster
articles.summary:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped in depth of 170 metres

Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal…
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu

blocks.text: Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped.

The workers were rescued during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst-affected by last week’s deadly Nepal floods, according to army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.

Sanjay Shah was the first to be rescued and was taken to the Nepal army barracks in Trishuli. Another person, identified as Kabir Maharjan, was also rescued from the tunnel. They were rescued from a depth of 170 metres inside the tunnel, confirmed Basnet.
Sanjay Shah was foreman at Upper Trishuli 3A and Kabir Maharjan was a superviser.
Nepal’s army released images of Shah being pulled from the small dark entrance of a tunnel. He emerged covered in mud but conscious and was carried from the site on a rescuer’s shoulder.
Speaking to army officials after he was rescued, Shah’s first question was: “What day is it?”
Describing his ordeal, Shah said he had been in the tunnel’s control room at the time of the flood.

“Usually there would be only five or six people there but at this time there must have been around 40 to 45 people inside,” he said. “Since I was in the control room, my responsibility was to save everyone’s lives. After such an accident, I couldn’t just run away by myself. I had to save everyone.
“While trying to get everyone out, I told them that there had been a major accident at the dam and urged everyone to run. In doing so, I lost time. In the end, I couldn’t get out myself.”
To keep himself calm in the darkness of the tunnel, Shah said he spent his time chanting mantras. He said that while trapped, he had been communicating with only three or four others.
“They were communicating by shouting to each other from nearby. There could also be people inside the powerhouse. Some of them may not have been able to escape,” he said.
Officials said the two men were in stable condition and flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.
Nepal’s communication minister, Bikram Timilsina, said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued. “We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people,”he wrote on social media.

Most of the hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers were destroyed when a surge of water, debris and mud came coursing down the valley last week, triggered by ‌the collapse of a melting glacier on the border between Nepal and China-controlled Tibet.

blocks.caption: A survivor is carried out after being rescued from inside the tunnel. Photograph: Nepal Army/Reuters

blocks.text: At least 1,287 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the Nepal’s disaster management agency.

Rescue efforts have increasingly centred on the hydropower tunnels, where authorities believe workers may ⁠have survived for more than a week due to air pockets. So far, more than 270 people have been rescued across several projects.

Large boulders and flood waters had deluged the hydropower tunnels, blocking off the entrances, and some were buried deep in mud. At the Upper Trishuli 3A facility, it took rescue workers almost six days to find the tunnels.

Army and specialist teams have been working round the clock to try and clear debris from the tunnel entrance. It was confirmed that voices of many people had been heard inside after a breakthrough was made on early Friday morning.
After the rescue team called out, “Don’t panic, we are rescuing you,” they received a response from inside: “OK.”

At least 557 workers are missing from the hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Families of those missing in the tunnels have been gathering at hospitals in Kathmandu and at the Nepal electricity office for nine days, desperate for answers about their relatives. Posters of workers missing in Trishuli 3A and other projects line the wall of Tribhuvan University teaching hospital in Nepal’s capital.
In total, local authorities estimate about 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects high up in the Himalayas, with about 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels.
Rescue efforts have also been focused on Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant where Nepal authorities said they are confident that 46 workers trapped in an underground chamber in the plant are still alive.

articles.title: UN to vote on adopting new world map that shows Africa’s true scale
articles.summary:
Togo-sponsored resolution calls to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland

The UN general assembly will vote on Friday on a resolution for the world to…

blocks.text: The UN general assembly will vote on Friday on a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.

Robert Dussey, Togo’s foreign affairs minister, said the resolution was sponsored by Togo and backed by countries including the African Union’s 54 other member states. He did not specify the total number.

blocks.caption: The 1569 map by Gerardus Mercator (1512-1594) has remained the global standard. Photograph: Stock Montage/Getty Images

blocks.text: “This discussion is not a political discussion [but] a scientific discussion, because there is scientific proof so we all have to accept the reality,” he said.

UN resolutions are non-enforceable but if the vote passes, it could lead to an update of classroom curriculums and everyday technology, given the wide usage of the Mercator projection in education, technology and governance.
The layout was introduced by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569 to help sailors navigate the seas. Almost five centuries later it remains the global standard.

Because of its projection style, however, regions near the equator appear significantly smaller than they are, whereas high-latitude areas look much larger. For example, the map shows Africa as being similar in size to Greenland, but the continent is 14 times larger than the Danish territory.

“You could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico and much of Europe into Africa and still have land to spare,” says a petition on Change.org for the #CorrectTheMap campaign, which has more than 11,000 signatures. The African Union endorsed the campaign in August 2025 and then asked Togo to spearhead its adoption.
Historians and geographers have said for years that the Mercator projection is rooted in western stereotypes. Activists have echoed this, with some coining the term “cartographic colonialism”.

Some argue that the map has subtly shaped international power dynamics by minimising the physical presence of the global south and visually inflating northern hemisphere nations while shrinking equatorial regions. This, they say, has reinforced systemic biases in international trade, development priorities and educational frameworks.

One of the Mercator projection’s most prominent critics was Arno Peters, a German historian, who launched the Peters world map based on the Gall–Peters projection in 1973. It has often been used as an alternative to the Mercator map.

blocks.caption: The 2018 Equal Earth Map. Photograph: equal-earth.com

blocks.text: Togo’s #CorrectTheMap campaign is promoting the use of the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design, which was developed by an international team of cartographers. Supporters say it will help to reverse perceptions of Africa and decolonise global curriculums.

Some analysts agree too. JJ Enoch, a London-based senior associate at JS Held, a geopolitical risk advisory firm, said the Mercator projection visually diminished Africa’s true scale. He linked the campaign to a quest by African nations for “greater influence in global institutions and greater control over how the continent is represented”.

He added: “Adopting an equal-area map … would provide a more accurate basis for education and public understanding, while signalling that Africa’s demographic, economic and geopolitical importance should no longer be viewed through inherited and distorted conventions.”

blocks.caption: A map of Africa from Mercator's atlas dating between 1595-1602. Photograph: Royal Geographical Society/Getty Images

blocks.text: Togolese authorities hope the vote will go the same way as another African Union-backed decision at the UN this year. In March a Ghana-sponsored resolution to describe the slave trade as “gravest crime against humanity” passed, with 123 states voting in favour. Three states voted no and 52 abstained.

Ghana’s success has given supporters of the map cause to believe in a favourable outcome. Togo’s government is planning an event in Lomé, the Togolese capital, with Unesco, the African Union and tech brands such as Google Maps during the first quarter of next year to map out the implementation of the resolution.
Dussey said: “To those who say why now, I say, why not? When we look at the world map … it is time for us to change the narrative.”
He added: “It’s time for us in Africa to take responsibility to change what we can change ourselves.”

articles.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence ‘whatsoever’ Morocco behind Ceuta border breach
articles.summary: Pedro Sánchez continues to defend Rabat after police report claiming border forces helped 70,000 cross border

blocks.text: Spain has seen no evidence “whatsoever” that Morocco planned or facilitated a mass border breach into its north African territory of Ceuta, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has told parliament.

The address on Thursday followed the emergence of a police report, commissioned by a judge and widely quoted in the media, claiming Moroccan border forces had actively aided about 70,000 people to cross the border in late July.

“I ‌can assure you ‌that no institution – not the diplomatic service, nor the European Commission, ‌nor any international body – has provided the Spanish government with any solid evidence that Morocco planned or carried out the incident. None whatsoever,” Sánchez told parliament.

Speaking the morning after about 50,000 people marched in Madrid to protest his handling of the Ceuta crisis, the socialist prime minister also denied the government had received any warning of the mass breach, saying no reports to authorities had anticipated “the scale or probability of what eventually happened”.

blocks.caption: A protest against the Spanish government’s handling of the recent border breach at Ceuta. Photograph: Francesco Militello Mirto/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Sánchez has repeatedly defended Morocco during the crisis, highlighting Rabat’s cooperation in returning most of the migrants in the days after the surge.

But he said on Thursday that Spain had summoned Morocco’s ambassador on 21 August because of “unacceptable statements” made by two ministers over Ceuta and Melilla, another Spanish north African territory. Last month, Morocco’s justice minister, Abdellatif Ouahbi, publicly reiterated Rabat’s sovereignty claims over the cities.
Sánchez said he had “for now” ruled out Moroccan government involvement but conceded that Moroccan forces had allowed crossings to occur during a key 10-hour period on 30 July.
Many of those who crossed said in interviews they had been actively encouraged to do so. Moroccan officials have denied enabling the crossing.
Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of the conservative People’s party, called on Sánchez to resign for his “incompetence and complicity”.

In response to Sánchez summoning the Moroccan ambassador to discuss the crisis, Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, said: “Morocco doesn’t need an ambassador in Spain – you are its ambassador.”

blocks.caption: People who entered Ceuta from Morocco in late July on hunger strike last month to demand asylum.  Photograph: Laura Rincon/EPA

blocks.text: As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter Ceuta at the end of July. The influx unleashed a political crisis, a humanitarian emergency and reignited tensions within the EU over immigration.

On Thursday, Sánchez appealed for European solidarity over the crisis. He did not single out any countries by name but, in a pointed passage apparently aimed at Italy and Denmark, the two countries that had led public criticism of Spain, said the principle of solidarity should apply to Ceuta as much as it applies to Greenland and Lampedusa.
Although 90% of the people had returned to Morocco within 24 hours, several thousand, including at least 500 minors, are thought to remain, either living on the street or in makeshift shelters.

Amid calls from Vox to return them to Morocco, Sánchez reminded parliament that under Spanish, European and international law, migrants had a right to be treated as individuals. “You can’t just grab someone by the arm and drag them across the frontier as though they were a sack of dirt,” he told MPs.

In reference to the hundreds of destitute minors, Aina Vidal of the leftwing group Sumar, said: “They’re children, not invaders, not soldiers. They didn’t come carrying bombs, they arrived wearing water wings, in tears.”

It seems likely the government will invest in facilities in Ceuta to accommodate the remaining migrants rather than risk the political backlash both in Spain and across Europe were they to bring them to the mainland.
There is also evidence that, faced with hunger as well as hostility from many local people, some migrants have already begun going back to Morocco.

However, as Sánchez told parliament, the per capita income of Ceuta is eight times that of Morocco and “even if we build a wall 100 metres high there will still be people prepared to throw themselves into the sea to get across”.
“We will not stop working until Ceuta emerges from this difficult situation: stronger, more prosperous, and more integrated with the rest of Spain and the EU,” he added.
Additional reporting by Jakub Krupa

articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says
articles.summary: About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu

blocks.text: Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber.
Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.

Most of the projects were destroyed when a surge of water, debris and mud came coursing down the river valley last week, triggered by ‌the collapse of a melting glacier on the border between Nepal and China-controlled Tibet.
The deadly flash floods reached up to 100mph (160km/h), according to scientists, and travelled more than 60 miles down the river valley, wiping away whole villages, bridges, and hydropower dams.
At least 1,252 people have been confirmed dead from the floods. More than 4,200 remain missing.

According to a preliminary estimate by the UN Development Programme, the disaster created at least 2.2m tonnes of debris, including parts of buildings, rocks and sediment. Large boulders and flood waters deluged the hydropower tunnels, blocking off the entrances, and some were buried deep in mud.

Rescue efforts have increasingly centred on these tunnels, where authorities believe workers may ⁠have survived for more than a week due to air pockets. So far, more than 270 people have been rescued from the hydropower projects.

blocks.caption: A turquoise-green house stands tall amid sludge near Trishuli River in the aftermath of flash floods.  Photograph: Arun Sankar/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Speaking on Wednesday, officials said they believed 46 people were still alive in an underground room in Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, and efforts were ongoing to locate them using excavators and other heavy equipment.

“We are very confident that they must be alive after one week because … they have food and water over there in the building,” Amhsu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal ⁠electricity authority, told Reuters.

Durga Gurung, 60, said his brother Jhappad Bhujel was among those trapped in a hydropower tunnel. “Right now, we are just relying on God,” he told the Guardian. “We have not been given any information about whether the people inside are alive or not.

“Neither the army nor the people from the electricity authority are telling us anything. So many days have passed that we have reached a point where it feels like all we can do is hope for a miracle.”
“Our relatives are sitting inside a dark tunnel,” he added. “How long can they possibly survive?”

blocks.caption: The area around Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant before the flash flood.  Photograph: Maxar/DigitalGlobe/Getty Images

blocks.text: Major rescue operations were under way or planned at four hydropower projects. Two sites – the Rasuwagadhi hydroelectric project and the Upper Trishuli 3A facility – where about 90 people are missing, offered the strongest prospect of finding survivors because of the presence of air inside the tunnels, Shahi said.

The Rasuwagadhi hydroelectric project is located in Rasuwa district, about three miles away from the border with Tibet, which was one of the areas of Nepal hardest hit by the floods, and remains almost inaccessible except by helicopter. “This is the only project where it’s possible to walk through ‌the tunnel,” Shahi said. “The army tried doing that three days ago, but they didn’t find the room. We are going in again.”

At the Upper Trishuli 3A facility, another project hit by the floods, it took rescue workers almost six days to find the tunnels ⁠because of the thick mud. The authorities believe about 30 to 40 people may still be alive in the tunnel. “We are expecting [survivors] in there because we ​are told there is a ​dry space inside. We are ​trying to break into the tunnel now,” said the Nepali army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet on Wednesday.

The army said the search and rescue operation would go on for as long as there was hope for survivors, but that efforts would also continue to recover the dead bodies. “We are using every technology ​available in Nepal ‌right now, and we ​are taking help ​from the Indians, Chinese, Koreans. We have experts from Australia too,” added Basnet.

Families of those still trapped in the projects have returned to the Nepal electricity office for the past eight days, in the hope for information. Laxmi Adhikari’s brother Jeevanlal Adhikari had gone to the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project to test the machines, when the floods hit.

She accused the authorities of withholding information from the families, and of not acting fast enough to save their relatives. “We have been running from one ministry to another and from disaster management authority to another government office, trying to find my brother,” she said. “We keep going from place to place, but the rescue operation has not been accelerated.”

She said the lack of answers made the wait even more painful: “When the water came rushing in, where did he go? Did he manage to get to safety? They haven’t even given us definite information about whether our people are alive or not.”

Nepal has invested more than $9bn (£6.7bn) in building hydropower dams across the mountains, huge sums given the country’s small economy. According to preliminary surveys, the floods debilitated or destroyed 11 hydropower plants and knocked out about 10% of Nepal’s total electricity-generation capacity.
According to the authorities, more than 20,000 houses will have to be rebuilt in the aftermath of the flood. Nepal has put the cost of recovery at more than $5bn (£3.7bn).

articles.title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest
articles.summary:
Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site

Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its…

blocks.text: Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India.

Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.

The coal-fired power station is situated near the Sundarbans, a Unesco world heritage site made up of more than 100 tiny islands across a river delta that supports hundreds of plant and animal species, including the Bengal tiger.

Sharif Jamil, an environmental campaigner based in the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka, who is one of the complainants, said heavy-metal pollution from the plant and the industrial development surrounding it was entering the Sundarbans through its interconnected rivers and canals.
“The Rampal power plant is right on the bank of the Pasur River, which is the lifeline of the Sundarbans,” he said. “The health of the forest is in trouble.”
Last November, a study found elevated levels of mercury and arsenic in water samples taken from the Sundarbans, with the highest concentrations recorded in the Pasur River.

Researchers identified industrial discharge and port-related activities among the sources of heavy-metal contamination and said the Rampal power station posed “a significant environmental threat due to emissions from coal combustion and increased navigation traffic”.

blocks.caption: The Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and one of the last habitats of Bengal tigers, supports the livelihoods of millions of people.  Photograph: Bengal Picture Library/Alamy

blocks.text: Millions of people live in the Sundarbans, and many depend on the river and forests for food and other resources.

The claimants allege that Barclays failed to conduct sufficient due diligence on the environmental and human rights risks before providing financial services to organisations connected to the project.

Barclays underwrote debt of India’s state-owned NTPC Ltd (formerly the National Thermal Power Corporation), one of the joint-venture partners behind the plant, according to King’s Legal Clinic, which is assisting the complainants. It also says Barclays underwrote bond issues for the Export-Import Bank of India between 2016 and 2019, which provided a loan for the Rampal project.

The complainants argue that emissions from the plant will contribute to global heating, rising sea levels and extreme weather in a region already highly vulnerable to the climate crisis. Mangroves act as a natural barrier against cyclones and other extreme weather.

The power station faced sustained opposition during its planning and construction, including concerns raised by Unesco in a report in 2016, which concluded that “air and water pollution have a high likelihood to irreversibly damage the … World Heritage property”. Some financial institutions, including banks in France, refused to support the project because of its potential environmental and social effects, the complaint says.

Jamil said Barclays’ international standing obliged it to consider the consequences of financing. “The greater your reputation, the greater your responsibility to behave responsibly towards the planet and its people,” he said. “Barclays is a reputed global organisation, and that is why it also has a responsibility.

“Other banks and financial institutions were divesting from, or declining to finance, this project,” he added. “Barclays and other financial organisations should change their policies and examine how their operations can protect the planet from climate catastrophe.”

Jamil also called on banks to direct more funding towards renewable energy rather than imported fossil fuels. “Bangladesh has sunlight throughout the year,” he said. “Why should we expand fossil fuels when there is enormous potential to produce electricity from renewable energy?”
The other complainants include Animesh Mandal, a farmer and politician, and the Dakshinbanga Matsyajibi Forum, a trade union representing fish workers in West Bengal.
They are being assisted by students and lawyers at King’s Human Rights and Environment Clinic, part of King’s College London’s law school.

Sue Willman, a solicitor at the clinic, said: “Rural communities in the Sundarbans are on the frontline of the climate and nature crisis. We hope to persuade banks and financial institutions to think again before financing oil and coal developments that are contributing to that crisis.”
The Office for Responsible Business Conduct, part of the Department for Business and Trade, will assess whether to consider the complaint.
Barclays Bank and BIFPCL (Bangladesh India Friendship Power Company Ltd), the holding company for the Maitree super thermal power project, declined to comment.

articles.title: New Canada tariffs on U.S. goods take effect, hitting nearly 700 products

image.caption: As small businesses open under Canada's latest round of retaliatory tariffs, many are weighing whether to absorb higher costs or pass them on to customers. (Michelle Both/CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New
Experts say Canada's new tariffs will have an outsized impact on the country's small and medium-sized businesses, with few consequences for individual consumers.
At 12:01 a.m. Tuesday, Canada hit $28 billion worth of U.S. imports with new dollar-for-dollar tariffs

Canadian businesses are opening Tuesday for the first time under the federal government's new dollar-for-dollar tariffs on $28 billion worth of U.S. imports. As many owners brace for higher costs and supply-chain issues, experts say consumers may not notice much impact.

The new levies took effect at 12:01 a.m. Tuesday, hitting nearly 700 American products at rates ranging from 15 per cent to 50 per cent. Affected items range from commodities such as steel and aluminum to household goods such as toilet paper and niche products including coin-operated arcade games.

The dollar-for-dollar tariffs are the federal government's response to the 50-per-cent levies imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump's administration on Aug. 22 on hundreds of products worth more than $28 billion — from plywood and cement to wine and hockey sticks.

Dan Kelly is president of the Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB), which represents more than 100,000 small and medium-sized firms across the country. He says this latest escalation in the trade war has some of his members feeling like their businesses have been deemed expendable by the government.
"They feel like they're ... cannon fodder in the trade war with the United States. That's not a good feeling," Kelly told CBC News.

"The previous rounds affected large commodities, and things like cars. This round is focused on my members, small and medium-sized business owners across Canada, who are in really rough shape right now."
Trump says Canadian dollar imbalance with U.S. is 'unacceptable'

JS Furniture is a Manitoba-based home furnishings and appliance retailer with locations in Winnipeg, Portage la Prairie, Steinbach and Winkler. General manager Brian Kyca estimates American goods account for 60 per cent of the company's sales by volume.
"What seems to be hit the hardest is going to be laminate-style bedroom suites," Kyca said in an interview.

"It seems the large items such as dressers, and chests, and drawers, are going to be subject to a 50 per cent tariff, and the smaller items, such as the headboards, footboard rails, night stands, and mirrors are going to be subject to 25 per cent."
According to Kyca, gauging the impact has been a frustrating and confusing ordeal, with only "vague" information available from agencies such as the Canada Border Services Agency.
For now, he said, JS Furniture plans to absorb the higher costs while trying to work out deals with manufacturers shipping U.S.-made goods into Canada.

"I've got people, customers that purchased stuff a month ago that are awaiting delivery, that could be subject now to tariffs. And I don't want to be the one that's going to phone our customers and say, 'Oh, by the way, this is going to cost more,'" Kyca said.
"We'll eat those costs, because it's not the customer's fault."
However, he acknowledged there's a limit to how long the company can hold the line on prices.
Colin Mang, an economics professor at McMaster University, said businesses across Canada are facing the same delicate balancing act.
"What we did see last year was that retailers absorbed about 75 per cent of the tariff cost, and only passed on a quarter of the cost to consumers," he said.

"This time around, it will depend on how long retailers expect tariffs to remain in place. If they believe that the tariffs are only going to be in for a short time, they're very likely to just absorb the costs again. Of course, that will mean a significant impact on their profitability."
New tariffs 'unlikely to affect most people in their day-to-day lives'
Last week, Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem weighed in on how the central bank expects Canada-U.S. tariffs to affect the economy.

"The counter-tariffs, and indeed the U.S. tariffs ... will add costs for some businesses," Macklem told reporters in Ottawa on Sept. 2. "These tariffs are very steep, but they are applied to a relatively narrow base."
"I'm feeling quite worried," CFIB president Kelly said. "The burden of counter-tariffs hits disproportionately hard on some, not on others."

Kyca said the Canada-U.S. trade war has put JS Furniture's plans to open more stores on hold. At the same time, he said the company's roughly 35 employees are starting to feel the impact, especially sales staff relying on commissions as consumers become more cautious with their spending.
"If people aren't coming in and buying furniture, they're not earning any money," Kyca said.
"People that do have disposable income are holding on to that money, and the people that are working day-to-day, cheque-to-cheque, are nickel-and-diming things," he added. "It's very frustrating."

Mang said Canada's new tariffs generally target U.S. goods with readily-available domestic alternatives. The idea, he says, is to give Canadian companies to an opportunity to capture a larger share of the domestic market, helping offset business lost in the U.S.
For consumers, he said, the situation isn't nearly as challenging.
"For the typical Canadian family, you're not gonna notice much of a difference because of these new counter-tariffs," Mang said.
"The key message is that this is unlikely to affect most people in their day-to-day lives."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. He was also a Columbia University energy journalism fellow for 2025.

articles.title: Avi Lewis's NDP is eyeing Toronto for its rebuild

image.caption: After last week's byelections, in which the NDP won zero seats, Leader Avi Lewis said: 'The big headline for me is we are back.' (Sean Kilpatrick/ The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

As NDP MPs meet in Toronto for their fall caucus retreat, the party is still in rough shape politically and financially. But Leader Avi Lewis and others say the New Democrat movement is ripe for a revival — and they think the city of Toronto offers a path forward.
5 elected members of the New Democrats are in Toronto for caucus retreat
As NDP MPs meet in Toronto for their fall caucus retreat, the party is still in rough shape politically and financially.

Federal New Democrats are digging themselves out of their election debt. Their leader still doesn't have a seat in the House of Commons. And their tiny caucus enters the fall Parliamentary sitting even smaller, after one MP joined the Liberals and another left.

But that's the one-sided view of the party held by those in the Ottawa political bubble, as NDP Leader Avi Lewis often likes to say. He and others say the New Democrat movement is ripe for a revival — and they think the city of Toronto offers a path forward.
'We are back,' Lewis says
In a video posted on social media the day after last week's byelections — in which the party won no seats — Lewis admitted the New Democrats were "never expected to win."

Nevertheless, Lewis said the results in Toronto signal the party is showing signs of coming back to life. In that byelection, the NDP saw their vote share triple compared to the 2025 general election in the Toronto riding of Beaches—East York.
"The big headline for me is we are back," Lewis said. "Our rebuild as a party is well underway. Lots of work still to do. But the early signs are really encouraging."

items: After more than 100 days as NDP leader, has Avi Lewis moved the needle?
Minister attacked museum's independence by calling for Palestinian wording changes, federal NDP leader says

blocks.text: Lewis said New Democrats did better in this "sleepy summer, somewhat cynical byelection," than they have in the past 11 years.
The 2025 general election was devastating for New Democrats with their worst-ever result. Jagmeet Singh resigned as leader on the spot.

In March, New Democrats elected Lewis, who won on the first ballot with 56 per cent of the vote. Six months in, and Lewis has yet to secure a seat in the House of Commons, opting not to run in the recent byelections or the six upcoming.
Lewis could run for a Toronto seat

A senior NDP source tells CBC the party's five-member caucus is going to Toronto because the party believes the path back to official party status is through Toronto seats, especially communities like Davenport and Parkdale.
CBC is not identifying the source as they are not authorized to speak publicly about internal party matters.

The city's downtown core and surrounding areas, the source said, is ground zero for the main issues Lewis has been focusing on — the cost of groceries, housing, opposing another West Coast pipeline and tackling the climate crisis.
The NDP hasn't won a seat in Toronto since 2011. But the party has potential, according to Éric Grenier, polling analyst and publisher of The Writ.

"I do think that the kind of messaging that Avi Lewis has been promoting, his general kind of approach and demeanour and policies are more likely to appeal in a place like Toronto, in urban downtown area kind of ridings."
'This trade war could and should hurt President Trump,' says NDP Leader Avi Lewis
Lewis told the independent news website The Breach he was tempted to run in the Beaches—East York byelection.
And CBC's source did leave open the potential that Lewis could eventually run in Canada's largest city.
"We're keeping our options open," the source said. "There are opportunities to win seats … there is real potential to build upon."
It would have been a gamble, but had Lewis run in Beaches—East York he could have won, said Jordan Leichnitz, a former NDP strategist and frequent panellist on CBC's Power and Politics.

Leichnitz said the votes the NDP were able to pick up likely came from progressive voters who are uncomfortable with Carney changing environmental regulations, building a pipeline and attempting to change the Canada Labour Code, potentially making it harder for some to strike.

"The ground organizing muscle that they were able to demonstrate in Beaches—East York is significant," said Leichnitz, who's also the Canada director for the Friedrich Ebert Stiftung, an international German foundation that's aligned with theSocial Democratic Party of Germany (SPD).

"And the fact that they were able to sort of prove, on the ground, the thesis that there are some progressive voters who voted Liberal who are now willing to come home under Lewis's leadership — that's important."
Can new NDP leader Avi Lewis unite the party?
Year-round organizing, not just elections

Under Lewis, the NDP is developing a model of permanent organizing where the party is training and connecting with volunteers throughout the year and not just during election time, according to Matthew Green, the party's outgoing national director.

At a time when many people have fewer in person social connections, he said, New Democrats hope NDP riding groups become community hubs where people form lasting relationships instead of just the transactional politics of door knocking and phone calls at election time.

"What we're proposing around building communities is the idea that there is space for joy and fun and socializing and community and food and music and dance and things that typically wouldn't be associated in the modern era with politics, but we're a core part of our CCF [Co-operative Commonwealth Federation; the NDP's political predecessor]."
Other than Beaches—East York, the NDP's byelection results were dismal for the NDP, according to Grenier.
Their vote share shrunk in Chicoutimi—Le Fjord and in North Vancouver—Capilano they earned three per cent of the vote and fell to third place, behind the Green Party of Canada.
"The NDP is still not in great shape. They're in better shape than they were in 2025, but that was the worst shape the party's ever been. So it's a low bar," Grenier said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

David Thurton is a senior reporter in CBC's Parliamentary Bureau. He covers daily politics in the nation’s capital and specializes in environment and energy policy. Born in Canada but raised in Trinidad and Tobago, he’s moved around more times than he can count. He’s worked for CBC in several provinces and territories, including Alberta and the Northwest Territories. He can be reached at david.thurton@cbc.ca
